I. Purpose and Scope 
 
A. Purpose  
1. The purpose of this Annex is to provide resources of member agencies to support 
emergency response needs in the Navajo County. 
B. Scope  
1. This Annex addresses both emergency assistance and the maintenance and mitigation 
efforts for responses specific to this Annex. Specifically, it discusses: 
  
2. Encompassed in this Annex is information on standard operating procedures (SOPs), 
movement of responders, victims and supplies associated with response and recover

<!-- page 880 -->
730  
efforts following a major disaster, egress and ingress information. Also included is 
information on major services by coordinating agencies critical to the welfare of the 
citizens of the Navajo County. 
II. Concept of Operations 
 
A. General  
1. This Annex is consistent with the Navajo County EOC's methodology, the requirements 
of the National Response Framework (NRF), the National Incident Management System 
(NIMS), and the Incident Command System (ICS). This structure and system supports 
incident assessment, planning, procurement, deployment, and coordination and support 
operations to the Navajo County through the Navajo County Emergency Policy Group, 
Area Operations and Regional Incident Management Teams (IMTs) to provide a timely 
and appropriate response to an emergency or situation. 
2. Procedures, protocols and plans for disaster response activities are to govern staff 
operations at the Navajo County EOC and in the field. These are in the form of the base 
plan and corresponding Appendices, ESF Annexes, Support Annexes, Threat 
Annexes, and Standard Operating Guidelines, which describe capabilities. Periodic 
training and exercises are also conducted to enhance effectiveness. 
3. In a large event requiring local or State mutual aid assistance, Annex will work with its 
support agency counterparts to seek and procure, plan, coordinate or direct the use of 
required assets. 
4. Throughout the response and recovery periods, these agencies will evaluate and 
analyze information requests to move people, materials, equipment and other resources 
as necessary. 
B. Direction and Control  
1. The Coordinating Agency is Navajo County Administrative Services / Navajo County 
Emergency Management / Navajo County Facilities Management / Navajo County 
Human Resources / Navajo County Information Technology / Navajo County Public 
Health Services District which is approved by the Arizona Department of Emergency and 
Military Affairs Cabinet Secretary, in coordination with local planning partners. The staff 
member serving as the Coordinator is appointed by and located in the Navajo County 
Administrative Services / Navajo County Emergency Management / Navajo County 
Facilities Management / Navajo County Human Resources / Navajo County Information 
Technology / Navajo County Public Health Services District. When support is necessary, 
the Coordinator coordinates all aspects of this Annex. 
2. This Annex complies with the National Response Framework (NRF), and the National 
Incident Management System (NIMS). The NIMS guides the direction and control 
system adopted by the Navajo County Emergency Management, which functions as the 
official disaster prevention, protection, response, preparedness, recovery, and mitigation 
organization within the Navajo County. 
3. It may operate at two levels: 1.) Navajo County EOC; and 2.) Field operations.

<!-- page 881 -->
731  
4. During emergency activations, all management decisions regarding transportation for 
the Navajo County are made at the Navajo County EOC by the coordinator. Under the 
Incident Command System (ICS) structure, the Planning, Logistics, Finance 
& Administration, and Operations Section and associated staff at the Navajo County 
EOC assist the incident commander in carrying out the overall mission. 
5. In accordance with a mission assignment, each primary and/or support organization 
assisting in the deployment of this Annex will retain administrative control over its own 
resources and personnel, but will be under the operational control of this Annex. Mission 
operational control may be delegated to the field by the Navajo County EOC. 
C. Organization  
1. County  
a. During an activation of the Navajo County EOC, primary and support agency 
staff are integrated with the Navajo County Administrative Services / Navajo 
County Emergency Management / Navajo County Facilities Management / 
Navajo County Human Resources / Navajo County Information Technology / 
Navajo County Public Health Services District staff to provide support. 
b. During an emergency or disaster event, the Navajo County EOC, Operations 
Section Chief will coordinate resource support with the Infrastructure Services 
Branch Chief. 
c. During the response phase, the Navajo County EOC will evaluate and analyze 
information regarding transportation services requests. This Annex will develop 
and update assessments of the transportation services status in the impacted 
area and undertake contingency planning to meet anticipated transportation 
requirements. 
d. The Navajo County Administrative Services / Navajo County Emergency 
Management / Navajo County Facilities Management / Navajo County Human 
Resources / Navajo County Information Technology / Navajo County Public 
Health Services District will develop and maintain the Annex and accompanying 
Appendices, Annexes and Standard Operating Guidelines that govern response 
actions related to emergencies. Primary and support agencies should develop 
and maintain their own similar documents for internal use, which must be 
compatible with and in support of the overall EOP. All such documents will be in 
compliance with the National Response Framework (NRF), The National Incident 
Management System (NIMS), the Incident Command System (ICS), and the 
Navajo County EOP. 
e. The Navajo County Administrative Services / Navajo County Emergency 
Management / Navajo County Facilities Management / Navajo County Human 
Resources / Navajo County Information Technology / Navajo County Public 
Health Services District shall be represented in the Annex most pertinent to the 
support of disaster intelligence collection and scope of response. 
2. State of Arizona

<!-- page 882 -->
732  
a. During an emergency or disaster event, the primary and support agencies at the 
will report to the Infrastructure Services Branch Chief, who reports to the 
Operations Section Chief under the overall direction of the State Emergency 
Operations Center (SEOC) Manager. 
b. The Arizona Department of Homeland Security & Emergency Management, 
reviews and maintains the overall actions of this Annex. Primary and support 
agencies should develop and maintain their own similar documents for internal 
use, which must be compatible with and in support of the overall Arizona 
Response Plan. All such documents will be in compliance with the National 
Response Framework (NRF), the National Incident Management System (NIMS), 
the Incident Command System (ICS) and the Arizona Response Plan. 
D. Alerts and Notifications  
1. The Navajo County Administrative Services / Navajo County Emergency Management / 
Navajo County Facilities Management / Navajo County Human Resources / Navajo 
County Information Technology / Navajo County Public Health Services District will notify 
the County Warning Point (Navajo County Governmental Complex) when information 
comes to their attention indicating that an emergency or disaster situation is developing. 
2. The County Warning Point (Navajo County Governmental Complex), will notify the on-
call Emergency Duty Officer or the Coordinator when the Navajo County has been 
threatened or impacted by an emergency or disaster event as provided in the County 
Warning Point procedure. 
3. This Annex will be activated or placed on standby upon notification by the Navajo 
County EOC. The representatives or designees of the coordinating agency will manage 
the emergency activities. If additional support is required, the coordinating and primary 
agencies may jointly manage activities. 
4. Upon instructions to activate or place staff on standby, Navajo County Administrative 
Services / Navajo County Emergency Management / Navajo County Facilities 
Management / Navajo County Human Resources / Navajo County Information 
Technology / Navajo County Public Health Services District will implement procedures to 
notify all planning team members and, if necessary, mobilize all personnel, facilities and 
physical resources likely to be needed, based on the emergency circumstance. 
E. Actions  
1. Actions carried out are grouped into phases of emergency management: Preparedness, 
Response, Recovery and Mitigation. Actions specifically designated for Vulnerable 
Needs populations are listed separately in conjunction with the Annex actions. Each 
phase requires specific skills and knowledge to accomplish the tasks and requires 
significant cooperation and collaboration between all agencies and the intended 
recipients of service.

IV. Financial Management 
 
A. This Annex is responsible for coordinating with Navajo County Finance Department to 
manage expenses relevant to an event. 
 
B. During a response, each agency and department fund disaster operations from their current 
operating budget and are responsible for recording and tracking agency expenditures. If a 
federally declared disaster exists, each agency is responsible for seeking reimbursement in 
accordance to the formula established by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) 
via the FEMA-State Agreement. 
 
C. Expenditures by support entities will be documented by those entities and submitted directly 
to the Navajo County Finance Department or a designated Finance Service officer as soon as 
possible.

<!-- page 900 -->
750  
V. References and Authorities 
 
REFERENCES 
1. Comprehensive Preparedness Guidance (CPG) 101, Developing and Maintaining 
Emergency Operations Plans, Version 3.0, September 2021. 
 
AUTHORITIES 
1. 44 CFR Part 13 - Uniform Administrative Requirements for Grants and Cooperative 
Agreements. 
2. 44 CFR Part 206 - Federal Disaster Assistance for Disasters Declared after November 
23, 1988. 
 
If Federal agencies become involved with any assistance during a disaster or emergency, 
a Presidential declared disaster is generally required which will be requested by the 
governor's office through the Cabinet Secretary of the Department of Homeland Security 
& Emergency Management. To understand this process more, it is described within 
FEMA Publication P-682 National Response Framework and FEMA Publication P-683. To 
obtain further information on the Federal assistance process and how it is structured you 
can find both of these publications in the File Archive portion of this living plan.

I. Purpose and Scope 
 
A. Purpose  
1. The purpose of this Annex is to provide resources of member agencies to support 
emergency response needs in the Navajo County. 
B. Scope  
1. This Annex addresses both emergency assistance and the maintenance and mitigation 
efforts for responses specific to this Annex. Specifically, it discusses:  
a.  
2. Encompassed in this Annex is information on standard operating procedures (SOPs), 
movement of responders, victims and supplies associated with response and recover

<!-- page 902 -->
752  
efforts following a major disaster, egress and ingress information. Also included is 
information on major services by coordinating agencies critical to the welfare of the 
citizens of the Navajo County. 
II. Concept of Operations 
 
A. General  
1. This Annex is consistent with the Navajo County EOC's methodology, the requirements 
of the National Response Framework (NRF), the National Incident Management System 
(NIMS), and the Incident Command System (ICS). This structure and system supports 
incident assessment, planning, procurement, deployment, and coordination and support 
operations to Navajo County through the Navajo County Emergency Policy Group, Area 
Operations and Regional Incident Management Teams (IMT) to provide a timely and 
appropriate response to an emergency or situation. 
2. Procedures, protocols and plans for disaster response activities are to govern staff 
operations at the Navajo County EOC and in the field. These are in the form of the base 
plan and corresponding Appendices, ESF Annexes, Support Annexes, Threat Annexes, 
and Standard Operating Guidelines, which describe capabilities. Periodic training and 
exercises are also conducted to enhance effectiveness. 
3. In a large event requiring local or State mutual aid assistance, Annex will work with its 
support agency counterparts to seek and procure, plan, coordinate and/or direct the use 
of required assets. 
4. Throughout the response and recovery periods, these agencies will evaluate and 
analyze information requests to move people, materials, equipment and other resources 
as necessary. 
B. Direction and Control  
1. The Coordinating Agency is Navajo County Attorney / Navajo County Emergency 
Management / Navajo County Facilities Management / Navajo County Flood Control 
District / Navajo County Human Resources / Navajo County Public Health Services 
District which is approved by the Arizona Department of Emergency and Military 
Affairs Cabinet Secretary, in coordination with local planning partners. The staff member 
serving as the Coordinator is appointed by and located in the Navajo County Attorney / 
Navajo County Emergency Management / Navajo County Facilities Management / 
Navajo County Flood Control District / Navajo County Human Resources / Navajo 
County Public Health Services District. When support is necessary, the Coordinator 
coordinates all aspects of this Annex. 
2. This Annex complies with the National Response Framework, and the National Incident 
Management System (NIMS). The NIMS guides the direction and control system 
adopted by the Navajo County Emergency Management, which functions as the official 
disaster prevention, protection, response, preparedness, recovery, and mitigation 
organization within the Navajo County. 
3. It may operate at two levels: 1.) Navajo County EOC; and 2.) Field operations.

<!-- page 903 -->
753  
4. During emergency activations, all management decisions regarding transportation for 
Navajo County are made at the Navajo County EOC by the coordinator. Under the 
Incident Command System structure, the Planning, Logistics, Finance/Administration, 
and Operations Section and associated staff at the Navajo County EOC assist the 
incident commander in carrying out the overall mission. 
5. In accordance with a mission assignment, each primary and/or support organization 
assisting in the deployment of this Annex will retain administrative control over its own 
resources and personnel, but will be under the operational control of this Annex. Mission 
operational control may be delegated to the field by the Navajo County EOC. 
C. Organization  
1. County  
a. During an activation of the Navajo County EOC, primary and support agency 
staff are integrated with the Navajo County Attorney / Navajo County Emergency 
Management / Navajo County Facilities Management / Navajo County Flood 
Control District / Navajo County Human Resources / Navajo County Public 
Health Services District staff to provide support. 
b. During an emergency or disaster event, the Navajo County EOC, Operations 
Section Chief will coordinate resource support with the Infrastructure Services 
Branch Chief. 
c. During the response phase, the Navajo County EOC will evaluate and analyze 
information regarding transportation services requests. This Annex will develop 
and update assessments of the transportation services status in the impacted 
area and undertake contingency planning to meet anticipated transportation 
requirements. 
d. The Navajo County Attorney / Navajo County Emergency Management / Navajo 
County Facilities Management / Navajo County Flood Control District / Navajo 
County Human Resources / Navajo County Public Health Services District will 
develop and maintain the Annex and accompanying Appendices, Annexes and 
Standard Operating Guidelines that govern response actions related to 
emergencies. Primary and support agencies should develop and maintain their 
own similar documents for internal use, which must be compatible with and in 
support of the overall EOP. All such documents will be in compliance with the 
National Response Framework (NRF), The National Incident Management 
System (NIMS), the Incident Command System (ICS), and the Navajo County 
EOP. 
e. The Navajo County Attorney / Navajo County Emergency Management / Navajo 
County Facilities Management / Navajo County Flood Control District / Navajo 
County Human Resources / Navajo County Public Health Services District shall 
be represented in the Annex most pertinent to the support of disaster intelligence 
collection and scope of response. 
2. State of Arizona

<!-- page 904 -->
754  
a. During an emergency or disaster event, the primary and support agencies at the 
will report to the Infrastructure Services Branch Chief, who reports to the 
Operations Section Chief under the overall direction of the State Emergency 
Operations Center (SEOC) Manager. 
b. The Arizona Department of Homeland Security & Emergency Management, 
reviews and maintains the overall actions of this Annex. Primary and support 
agencies should develop and maintain their own similar documents for internal 
use, which must be compatible with and in support of the overall Arizona 
Response Plan. All such documents will be in compliance with the National 
Response Framework, the National Incident Management System, the Incident 
Command System and the Arizona Response Plan. 
D. Alerts and Notifications  
1. The Navajo County Attorney / Navajo County Emergency Management / Navajo County 
Facilities Management / Navajo County Flood Control District / Navajo County Human 
Resources / Navajo County Public Health Services District will notify the County Warning 
Point (Navajo County Governmental Complex) when information comes to their attention 
indicating that an emergency or disaster situation is developing. 
2. The County Warning Point (Navajo County Governmental Complex), will notify the on-
call Emergency Duty Officer or the Coordinator when the Navajo County has been 
threatened or impacted by an emergency or disaster event as provided in the County 
Warning Point procedure. 
3. This Annex will be activated or placed on standby upon notification by the Navajo 
County EOC. The representatives or designees of the coordinating agency will manage 
the emergency activities. If additional support is required, the coordinating and primary 
agencies may jointly manage activities. 
4. Upon instructions to activate or place staff on standby, Navajo County Attorney / Navajo 
County Emergency Management / Navajo County Facilities Management / Navajo 
County Flood Control District / Navajo County Human Resources / Navajo County Public 
Health Services District will implement procedures to notify all planning team members 
and, if necessary, mobilize all personnel, facilities and physical resources likely to be 
needed, based on the emergency circumstance. 
E. Actions  
1. Actions carried out are grouped into phases of emergency management: Preparedness, 
Response, Recovery and Mitigation. Actions specifically designated for Vulnerable 
Needs populations are listed separately in conjunction with the Annex actions. Each 
phase requires specific skills and knowledge to accomplish the tasks and requires 
significant cooperation and collaboration between all agencies and the intended 
recipients of service. 
III. Responsibilities

Preparedness (Pre-Event) Actions for Support Annex C - Worker Safety and Health 
1 Update Ready Navajo County employee emergency alerting system. 
Response (During Event) Actions for Support Annex C - Worker Safety and Health 
1 Quickly lock exterior doors and close windows, air vents. 
2 
Write down the names of everyone in the room, and call your designated emergency 
contact to report who is in the room with you, and their affiliation with your department 
(employee, visitor, client, customer). 
3 Evacuate building and gather at designated safe zone 
   
Coordinating: Navajo County Emergency Management 
Preparedness (Pre-Event) Actions for Support Annex C - Worker Safety and Health 
1 Identify specific health and safety risks for disasters. 
2 
Gather essential disaster supplies, such as nonperishable food, bottled water, battery-
powered radios, first-aid supplies, flashlights, batteries, duct tape, plastic sheeting, and 
plastic garbage bags. 
3 
Select interior room(s) above the ground floor, with the fewest windows or vents. The 
room(s) should have adequate space for everyone to be able to sit. Avoid overcrowding by 
selecting several rooms if necessary. Large storage closets, utility rooms, pantries, copy 
and conference rooms without exterior windows will work well. Avoid selecting a room with 
mechanical equipment like ventilation blowers or pipes, because this equipment may not 
be able to be sealed from the outdoors. 
4 Update Ready Navajo County employee emergency alerting system. 
5 Train employees on "Run, Hide, Fight" https://www.fbi.gov/about-us/office-of-partner-
engagement/active-shooter-incidents/run-hide-fight-video

(employee, visitor, client, customer). 
3 Evacuate building and gather at designated safe zone 
4 Report emergencies to 911.

IV. Financial Management 
 
A. This Annex is responsible for coordinating with Navajo County Finance Department to 
manage expenses relevant to an event. 
 
B. During a response, each agency/department fund disaster operations from their current 
operating budget and are responsible for recording and tracking agency expenditures. If a 
federally declared disaster exists, each agency is responsible for seeking reimbursement in 
accordance to the formula established by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) 
via the FEMA-State Agreement.

<!-- page 923 -->
773  
 
C. Expenditures by support entities will be documented by those entities and submitted directly 
to the Navajo County Finance Department or a designated Finance Service officer as soon as 
possible. 
V. References and Authorities 
 
REFERENCES 
1. Comprehensive Preparedness Guidance (CPG) 101, Developing and Maintaining 
Emergency Operations Plans, Version 3.0, September 2021. 
 
AUTHORITIES 
1. 44 CFR Part 13 - Uniform Administrative Requirements for Grants and Cooperative 
Agreements. 
2. 44 CFR Part 206 - Federal Disaster Assistance for Disasters Declared after November 
23, 1988. 
 
If Federal agencies become involved with any assistance during a disaster or emergency, 
a Presidential declared disaster is generally required which will be requested by the 
governor's office through the Cabinet Secretary of the Department of Homeland Security 
& Emergency Management. To understand this process more, it is described within 
FEMA Publication P-682 National Response Framework and FEMA Publication P-683. To 
obtain further information on the Federal assistance process and how it is structured you 
can find both of these publications in the File Archive portion of this living plan.

I. Purpose and Scope 
 
A. Purpose  
1. The purpose of this Annex is to provide resources of member agencies to support 
emergency response needs in the Navajo County. 
B. Scope  
1. This Annex addresses both emergency assistance and the maintenance and mitigation 
efforts for responses specific to this Annex. Specifically, it discusses: 
  
2. Encompassed in this Annex is information on standard operating procedures (SOPs), 
movement of responders, victims and supplies associated with response and recover 
efforts following a major disaster, egress and ingress information. Also included is 
information on major services by coordinating agencies critical to the welfare of the 
citizens of the Navajo County.

<!-- page 925 -->
775  
II. Concept of Operations 
 
A. General  
1. This Annex is consistent with the Navajo County EOC's methodology, the requirements 
of the National Response Framework (NRF), the National Incident Management System 
(NIMS), and the Incident Command System (ICS). This structure and system supports 
incident assessment, planning, procurement, deployment, and coordination and support 
operations to the Navajo County through the Navajo County Emergency Policy Group, 
Area Operations and Regional Incident Management Teams (IMTs) to provide a timely 
and appropriate response to an emergency or situation. 
2. Procedures, protocols and plans for disaster response activities are to govern staff 
operations at the Navajo County EOC and in the field. These are in the form of the base 
plan and corresponding Appendices, ESF Annexes, Support Annexes, Threat Annexes, 
and Standard Operating Guidelines, which describe capabilities. Periodic training and 
exercises are also conducted to enhance effectiveness. 
3. In a large event requiring local or State mutual aid assistance, Support Annex D will 
work with its support agency counterparts to seek and procure, plan, coordinate and/or 
direct the use of required assets. 
4. Throughout the response and recovery periods, these agencies will evaluate and 
analyze information requests to move people, materials, equipment and other resources 
as necessary. 
B. Direction and Control  
1. The Coordinating Agency is BIA Fort Apache Agency / White Mountain Apache Fire and 
Rescue which is approved by the Arizona Department of Emergency and Military 
Affairs Cabinet Secretary, in coordination with local planning partners. The staff member 
serving as the Coordinator is appointed by and located in the BIA Fort Apache Agency / 
White Mountain Apache Fire and Rescue. When support is necessary, the Coordinator 
coordinates all aspects of this Annex. 
2. This Annex complies with the National Response Framework (NRF), and the National 
Incident Management System (NIMS). The NIMS guides the direction and control 
system adopted by the Navajo County Emergency Management, which functions as the 
official disaster prevention, protection, response, preparedness, recovery, and mitigation 
organization within Navajo County. 
3. It may operate at two levels: 1.) Navajo County EOC; and 2.) Field operations. 
4. During emergency activations, all management decisions regarding transportation for 
the Navajo County are made at the Navajo County EOC by the coordinator. Under the 
Incident Command System structure, the Planning, Logistics, Finance & Administration, 
and Operations Section and associated staff at the Navajo County EOC assist the 
incident commander in carrying out the overall mission.

<!-- page 926 -->
776  
5. In accordance with a mission assignment, each primary or support organization assisting 
in the deployment of this Annex will retain administrative control over its own resources 
and personnel, but will be under the operational control of this Annex. Mission 
operational control may be delegated to the field by the Navajo County EOC. 
C. Organization  
1. County  
a. During an activation of the Navajo County EOC, primary and support agency 
staff are integrated with the BIA Fort Apache Agency / White Mountain Apache 
Fire and Rescue staff to provide support. 
b. During an emergency or disaster event, the Navajo County EOC, Operations 
Section Chief will coordinate resource support with the Infrastructure Services 
Branch Chief. 
c. During the response phase, the Navajo County EOC will evaluate and analyze 
information regarding transportation services requests. This Annex will develop 
and update assessments of the transportation services status in the impacted 
area and undertake contingency planning to meet anticipated transportation 
requirements. 
d. The BIA Fort Apache Agency / White Mountain Apache Fire and Rescue will 
develop and maintain the Annex and accompanying Appendices, Annexes and 
Standard Operating Guidelines that govern response actions related to 
emergencies. Primary and support agencies should develop and maintain their 
own similar documents for internal use, which must be compatible with and in 
support of the overall EOP. All such documents will be in compliance with the 
National Response Framework (NRF), The National Incident Management 
System (NIMS), the Incident Command System (ICS), and the Navajo County 
EOP. 
e. The BIA Fort Apache Agency / White Mountain Apache Fire and Rescue shall be 
represented in the Annex most pertinent to the support of disaster intelligence 
collection and scope of response. 
2. State of Arizona   
a. During an emergency or disaster event, the primary and support agencies at the 
will report to the Infrastructure Services Branch Chief, who reports to the 
Operations Section Chief under the overall direction of the State Emergency 
Operations Center (SEOC) Manager. 
b. The Arizona Department of Homeland Security & Emergency Management, 
reviews and maintains the overall actions of this Annex. Primary and support 
agencies should develop and maintain their own similar documents for internal 
use, which must be compatible with and in support of the overall Arizona 
Response Plan. All such documents will be in compliance with the National 
Response Framework (NRF), the National Incident Management System (NIMS), 
the Incident Command System (ICS) and the Arizona Response Plan.

<!-- page 927 -->
777  
D. Alerts and Notifications  
1. The BIA Fort Apache Agency / White Mountain Apache Fire and Rescue will notify the 
County Warning Point (Navajo County Governmental Complex) when information comes 
to their attention indicating that an emergency or disaster situation is developing. 
2. The County Warning Point (Navajo County Governmental Complex), will notify the on-
call Emergency Duty Officer and/or the Coordinator when the Navajo County has been 
threatened or impacted by an emergency or disaster event as provided in the County 
Warning Point procedure. 
3. This Annex will be activated or placed on standby upon notification by the Navajo 
County EOC. The representatives or designees of the coordinating agency will manage 
the emergency activities. If additional support is required, the coordinating and primary 
agencies may jointly manage activities. 
4. Upon instructions to activate or place staff on standby, BIA Fort Apache Agency / White 
Mountain Apache Fire and Rescue will implement procedures to notify all planning team 
members and, if necessary, mobilize all personnel, facilities and physical resources 
likely to be needed, based on the emergency circumstance. 
E. Actions  
1. Actions carried out are grouped into phases of emergency management: Preparedness, 
Response, Recovery and Mitigation. Actions specifically designated for Vulnerable 
Needs populations are listed separately in conjunction with the Annex actions. Each 
phase requires specific skills and knowledge to accomplish the tasks and requires 
significant cooperation and collaboration between all agencies and the intended 
recipients of service.

1 
• The Division of Emergency Management (ADEM) in cooperation with other

Response (During Event) Actions for Support Annex D - Tribal Relations 
1 
• Maintains primary responsibility for implementing consistent tribal relations 
policies and procedures during potential or actual incidents of statewide or 
national significance. 
2 
• Responsible for coordinating data-sharing by other agencies and departments 
that have responsibilities for collecting and maintaining data relevant to incident 
management for incidents that involve tribes. 
3 
• Responsible for coordinating and designating staff for the Tribal Relations 
Element at the SEOC. The Tribal Relations Element may include representatives 
from other departments and agencies, as appropriate and as jurisdictions dictate.  
4 
• Be responsible for coordinating tribal resources to address the full spectrum of 
actions to prevent, prepare for, respond to, and recover from incidents involving 
all hazards and incidents. including terrorism, natural disasters, accidents, and 
other contingencies. 
5 • Maintain extraordinary powers to suspend tribal laws and ordinances, such as to 
establish a curfew, direct evacuations, and order a quarantine. 
6 
• Provide leadership and play a key role in communicating to the tribal nation, and 
in helping people, businesses, and organizations cope with the consequences of 
any type of domestic incident within the tribe’s jurisdiction. 
7 • Negotiate and enter into mutual aid agreements with other tribes/jurisdictions to 
facilitate resource-sharing. 
8 • Request State and/or Federal assistance through the Governor of the State when 
the tribe’s capabilities have been exceeded or exhausted. 
9 
• The Governor must request a Presidential disaster declaration on behalf of a tribe 
under the Stafford Act; however, State/Federal departments and agencies can 
work directly with tribes within existing agency authorities and resources in the 
absence of such a declaration.

<!-- page 930 -->
780  
10 
• State departments and agencies comply with existing Federal laws and Executive 
orders mandating that the government deal with Indian tribes on a government-to-
government basis, reflecting the federally recognized tribes’ right of self-
government as sovereign domestic dependent nations. A tribe may, however, opt 
to and is encouraged to deal directly with State and county officials. 
11 
• State departments and agencies requested to participate in potential or actual 
incident response on tribal lands and consult and/or collaborate with tribal 
governments on matters affecting the tribes and must be aware of the social, 
political, and cultural aspects of an incident area that might affect incident 
management operations. 
12 
• State departments and agencies provide appropriate incident management 
officials with access to current databases containing information on tribal 
resources, demographics, and geospatial information.

I. Purpose and Scope 
 
A. Purpose  
1. The purpose of this Annex is to provide resources of member agencies to support 
emergency response needs in the Navajo County. 
B. Scope  
1. This Annex addresses both emergency assistance and the maintenance and mitigation 
efforts for responses specific to this Annex. Specifically, it discusses: 
  
2. Encompassed in this Annex is information on standard operating procedures (SOPs), 
movement of responders, victims and supplies associated with response and recover

<!-- page 935 -->
785  
efforts following a major disaster, egress and ingress information. Also included is 
information on major services by coordinating agencies critical to the welfare of the 
citizens of the Navajo County. 
II. Concept of Operations 
 
A. General  
1. This Annex is consistent with the Navajo County EOC's methodology, the requirements 
of the National Response Framework (NRF), the National Incident Management System 
(NIMS), and the Incident Command System (ICS). This structure and system supports 
incident assessment, planning, procurement, deployment, and coordination and support 
operations to the Navajo County through the Navajo County Emergency Policy Group, 
Area Operations and Regional Incident Management Teams (IMT) to provide a timely 
and appropriate response to an emergency or situation. 
2. Procedures, protocols and plans for disaster response activities are to govern staff 
operations at the Navajo County EOC and in the field. These are in the form of the base 
plan and corresponding Appendices, ESF Annexes, Support Annexes, Threat Annexes, 
and Standard Operating Guidelines, which describe capabilities. Periodic training and 
exercises are also conducted to enhance effectiveness. 
3. In a large event requiring local or State mutual aid assistance, Annex will work with its 
support agency counterparts to seek and procure, plan, coordinate or direct the use of 
required assets. 
4. Throughout the response and recovery periods, these agencies will evaluate and 
analyze information requests to move people, materials, equipment and other resources 
as necessary. 
B. Direction and Control  
1. The Coordinating Agency is BNSF Railway / Navajo County Emergency Management 
which is approved by the Arizona Department of Emergency and Military Affairs Cabinet 
Secretary, in coordination with local planning partners. The staff member serving as the 
Coordinator is appointed by and located in the BNSF Railway / Navajo County 
Emergency Management. When support is necessary, the Coordinator coordinates all 
aspects of this Annex. 
2. This Annex complies with the National Response Framework (NRF), and the National 
Incident Management System (NIMS). The NIMS guides the direction and control 
system adopted by the Navajo County Emergency Management, which functions as the 
official disaster prevention, protection, response, preparedness, recovery, and mitigation 
organization within Navajo County. 
3. It may operate at two levels: 1.) Navajo County EOC; and 2.) Field operations. 
4. During emergency activations, all management decisions regarding transportation for 
the Navajo County are made at the Navajo County EOC by the coordinator. Under the 
Incident Command System structure, the Planning, Logistics, Finance & Administration,

<!-- page 936 -->
786  
and Operations Section and associated staff at the Navajo County EOC assist the 
incident commander in carrying out the overall mission. 
5. In accordance with a mission assignment, each primary and/or support organization 
assisting in the deployment of this Annex will retain administrative control over its own 
resources and personnel, but will be under the operational control of this Annex. Mission 
operational control may be delegated to the field by the Navajo County EOC. 
C. Organization  
1. County  
a. During an activation of the Navajo County EOC, primary and support agency 
staff are integrated with the BNSF Railway / Navajo County Emergency 
Management staff to provide support. 
b. During an emergency or disaster event, the Navajo County EOC, Operations 
Section Chief will coordinate resource support with the Infrastructure Services 
Branch Chief. 
c. During the response phase, the Navajo County EOC will evaluate and analyze 
information regarding transportation services requests. This Annex will develop 
and update assessments of the transportation services status in the impacted 
area and undertake contingency planning to meet anticipated transportation 
requirements. 
d. The BNSF Railway / Navajo County Emergency Management will develop and 
maintain the Annex and accompanying Appendices, Annexes and Standard 
Operating Guidelines that govern response actions related to emergencies. 
Primary and support agencies should develop and maintain their own similar 
documents for internal use, which must be compatible with and in support of the 
overall EOP. All such documents will be in compliance with the National 
Response Framework (NRF), The National Incident Management System 
(NIMS), the Incident Command System (ICS), and the Navajo County EOP. 
e. The BNSF Railway / Navajo County Emergency Management shall be 
represented in the Annex most pertinent to the support of disaster intelligence 
collection and scope of response. 
2. State of Arizona   
a. During an emergency or disaster event, the primary and support agencies at the 
will report to the Infrastructure Services Branch Chief, who reports to the 
Operations Section Chief under the overall direction of the State Emergency 
Operations Center (SEOC) Manager. 
b. The Arizona Department of Homeland Security & Emergency Management, 
reviews and maintains the overall actions of this Annex. Primary and support 
agencies should develop and maintain their own similar documents for internal 
use, which must be compatible with and in support of the overall Arizona 
Response Plan. All such documents will be in compliance with the National

<!-- page 937 -->
787  
Response Framework (NRF), the National Incident Management System (NIMS), 
the Incident Command System (ICS) and the Arizona Response Plan. 
D. Alerts and Notifications  
1. The BNSF Railway / Navajo County Emergency Management will notify the County 
Warning Point (Navajo County Governmental Complex) when information comes to their 
attention indicating that an emergency or disaster situation is developing. 
2. The County Warning Point (Navajo County Governmental Complex), will notify the on-
call Emergency Duty Officer and/or the Coordinator when the Navajo County has been 
threatened or impacted by an emergency or disaster event as provided in the County 
Warning Point procedure. 
3. This Annex will be activated or placed on standby upon notification by the Navajo 
County EOC. The representatives or designees of the coordinating agency will manage 
the emergency activities. If additional support is required, the coordinating and primary 
agencies may jointly manage activities. 
4. Upon instructions to activate or place staff on standby, BNSF Railway / Navajo County 
Emergency Management will implement procedures to notify all planning team members 
and, if necessary, mobilize all personnel, facilities and physical resources likely to be 
needed, based on the emergency circumstance. 
E. Actions  
1. Actions carried out are grouped into phases of emergency management: Preparedness, 
Response, Recovery and Mitigation. Actions specifically designated for Vulnerable 
Needs populations are listed separately in conjunction with the Annex actions. Each 
phase requires specific skills and knowledge to accomplish the tasks and requires 
significant cooperation and collaboration between all agencies and the intended 
recipients of service.

IV. Financial Management 
 
A. This Annex is responsible for coordinating with Navajo County Finance Department to 
manage expenses relevant to an event. 
 
B. During a response, each agency and department fund disaster operations from their current 
operating budget and are responsible for recording and tracking agency expenditures. If a 
Federally declared disaster exists, each agency is responsible for seeking reimbursement in 
accordance to the formula established by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) 
via the FEMA-State Agreement. 
 
C. Expenditures by support entities will be documented by those entities and submitted directly 
to the Navajo County Finance Department or a designated Finance Service officer as soon as 
possible.

I. Purpose and Scope 
 
A. Purpose  
1. The purpose of this Annex is to provide resources of member agencies to support 
emergency response needs in the Navajo County. 
B. Scope  
1. This Annex addresses both emergency assistance and the maintenance and mitigation 
efforts for responses specific to this Annex. Specifically, it discusses: 
  
2. Encompassed in this Annex is information on standard operating procedures (SOP), 
movement of responders, victims and supplies associated with response and recover 
efforts following a major disaster, egress and ingress information. Also included is 
information on major services by coordinating agencies critical to the welfare of the 
citizens of the Navajo County. 
II. Concept of Operations 
 
A. General

<!-- page 950 -->
800  
1. This Annex is consistent with the Navajo County EOC's methodology, the requirements 
of the National Response Framework (NRF), the National Incident Management System 
(NIMS), and the Incident Command System (ICS). This structure and system supports 
incident assessment, planning, procurement, deployment, and coordination and support 
operations to the Navajo County through the Navajo County Emergency Policy Group, 
Area Operations and Regional Incident Management Teams (IMT) to provide a timely 
and appropriate response to an emergency or situation. 
2. Procedures, protocols and plans for disaster response activities are to govern staff 
operations at the Navajo County EOC and in the field. These are in the form of the base 
plan and corresponding Appendices, ESF Annexes, Support Annexes, Threat 
Annexes, and Standard Operating Guidelines, which describe capabilities. Periodic 
training and exercises are also conducted to enhance effectiveness. 
3. In a large event requiring local or State mutual aid assistance, Annex will work with its 
support agency counterparts to seek and procure, plan, coordinate or direct the use of 
required assets. 
4. Throughout the response and recovery periods, these agencies will evaluate and 
analyze information requests to move people, materials, equipment and other resources 
as necessary. 
B. Direction and Control  
1. The Coordinating Agency is Navajo County Emergency Management / Navajo County 
Public Health Services District which is approved by the Arizona Department of 
Emergency and Military Affairs Cabinet Secretary, in coordination with local planning 
partners. The staff member serving as the Coordinator is appointed by and located in the 
Navajo County Emergency Management / Navajo County Public Health Services 
District. When support is necessary, the Coordinator coordinates all aspects of this 
Annex. 
2. This Annex complies with the National Response Framework (NRF), and the National 
Incident Management System (NIMS). The NIMS guides the direction and control 
system adopted by the Navajo County Emergency Management, which functions as the 
official disaster prevention, protection, response, preparedness, recovery, and mitigation 
organization within the Navajo County. 
3. It may operate at two levels: 1.) Navajo County EOC; and 2.) Field operations. 
4. During emergency activations, all management decisions regarding transportation for 
the Navajo County are made at the Navajo County EOC by the coordinator. Under the 
Incident Command System (ICS) structure, the Planning, Logistics, Finance 
& Administration, and Operations Section and associated staff at the Navajo County 
EOC assist the incident commander in carrying out the overall mission. 
5. In accordance with a mission assignment, each primary and/or support organization 
assisting in the deployment of this Annex will retain administrative control over its own 
resources and personnel, but will be under the operational control of this Annex. Mission 
operational control may be delegated to the field by the Navajo County EOC.

<!-- page 951 -->
801  
C. Organization  
1. County  
1. During an activation of the Navajo County EOC, primary and support agency 
staff are integrated with the Navajo County Emergency Management / Navajo 
County Public Health Services District staff to provide support. 
2. During an emergency or disaster event, the Navajo County EOC, Operations 
Section Chief will coordinate resource support with the Infrastructure Services 
Branch Chief. 
3. During the response phase, the Navajo County EOC will evaluate and analyze 
information regarding transportation services requests. This Annex will develop 
and update assessments of the transportation services status in the impacted 
area and undertake contingency planning to meet anticipated transportation 
requirements. 
4. The Navajo County Emergency Management / Navajo County Public Health 
Services District will develop and maintain the Annex and accompanying 
Appendices, Annexes and Standard Operating Guidelines that govern response 
actions related to emergencies. Primary and support agencies should develop 
and maintain their own similar documents for internal use, which must be 
compatible with and in support of the overall EOP. All such documents will be in 
compliance with the National Response Framework (NRF), The National Incident 
Management System (NIMS), the Incident Command System (ICS), and the 
Navajo County EOP. 
5. The Navajo County Emergency Management / Navajo County Public Health 
Services District shall be represented in the Annex most pertinent to the support 
of disaster intelligence collection and scope of response. 
2. State of Arizona   
1. During an emergency or disaster event, the primary and support agencies at the 
will report to the Infrastructure Services Branch Chief, who reports to the 
Operations Section Chief under the overall direction of the State Emergency 
Operations Center (SEOC) Manager. 
2. The Arizona Department of Homeland Security & Emergency Management, 
reviews and maintains the overall actions of this Annex. Primary and support 
agencies should develop and maintain their own similar documents for internal 
use, which must be compatible with and in support of the overall Arizona 
Response Plan. All such documents will be in compliance with the National 
Response Framework (NRF), the National Incident Management System (NIMS), 
the Incident Command System (ICS) and the Arizona Response Plan. 
D. Alerts and Notifications  
1. The Navajo County Emergency Management / Navajo County Public Health Services 
District will notify the County Warning Point (Navajo County Governmental

<!-- page 952 -->
802  
Complex) when information comes to their attention indicating that an emergency or 
disaster situation is developing. 
2. The County Warning Point (Navajo County Governmental Complex), will notify the on-
call Emergency Duty Officer or the Coordinator when Navajo County has been 
threatened or impacted by an emergency or disaster event as provided in the County 
Warning Point procedure. 
3. This Annex will be activated or placed on standby upon notification by the Navajo 
County EOC. The representatives or designees of the coordinating agency will manage 
the emergency activities. If additional support is required, the coordinating and primary 
agencies may jointly manage activities. 
4. Upon instructions to activate or place staff on standby, Navajo County Emergency 
Management / Navajo County Public Health Services District will implement procedures 
to notify all planning team members and, if necessary, mobilize all personnel, facilities 
and physical resources likely to be needed, based on the emergency circumstance. 
E. Actions  
1. Actions carried out are grouped into phases of emergency management: Preparedness, 
Response, Recovery and Mitigation. Actions specifically designated for Vulnerable 
Needs populations are listed separately in conjunction with the Annex actions. Each 
phase requires specific skills and knowledge to accomplish the tasks and requires 
significant cooperation and collaboration between all agencies and the intended 
recipients of service.

A. This Annex is responsible for coordinating with Navajo County Finance Department to 
manage expenses relevant to an event.

operating budget and are responsible for recording and tracking agency expenditures. If a 
federally declared disaster exists, each agency is responsible for seeking reimbursement in 
accordance to the formula established by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) 
via the FEMA-State Agreement.

to the Navajo County Finance Department or a designated Finance Service officer as soon as

emergency response needs in the Navajo County.

1. This Annex addresses both emergency assistance and the maintenance and mitigation 
efforts for responses specific to this Annex. Specifically, it discusses: 
  
2. Encompassed in this Annex is information on standard operating procedures (SOP), 
movement of responders, victims and supplies associated with response and recover 
efforts following a major disaster, egress and ingress information. Also included is 
information on major services by coordinating agencies critical to the welfare of the 
citizens of the Navajo County. 
II. Concept of Operations 
 
A. General  
1. This Annex is consistent with the Navajo County EOC's methodology, the requirements 
of the National Response Framework (NRF), the National Incident Management System 
(NIMS), and the Incident Command System (ICS). This structure and system supports

<!-- page 967 -->
817  
incident assessment, planning, procurement, deployment, and coordination and support 
operations to the Navajo County through the Navajo County Emergency Policy Group, 
Area Operations and Regional Incident Management Teams (IMT) to provide a timely 
and appropriate response to an emergency or situation. 
2. Procedures, protocols and plans for disaster response activities are to govern staff 
operations at the Navajo County EOC and in the field. These are in the form of the base 
plan and corresponding Appendices, ESF Annexes, Support Annexes, Threat 
Annexes, and Standard Operating Guidelines, which describe capabilities. Periodic 
training and exercises are also conducted to enhance effectiveness. 
3. In a large event requiring local or State mutual aid assistance, Annex will work with its 
support agency counterparts to seek and procure, plan, coordinate or direct the use of 
required assets. 
4. Throughout the response and recovery periods, these agencies will evaluate and 
analyze information requests to move people, materials, equipment and other resources 
as necessary. 
B. Direction and Control  
1. The Coordinating Agency is FBI Pinetop-Lakeside / Navajo County Emergency 
Management / Navajo County Information Technology / Navajo County Sheriff's Office 
which is approved by the Arizona Department of Emergency and Military Affairs Cabinet 
Secretary, in coordination with local planning partners. The staff member serving as the 
Coordinator is appointed by and located in the FBI Pinetop-Lakeside / Navajo County 
Emergency Management / Navajo County Information Technology / Navajo County 
Sheriff's Office. When support is necessary, the Coordinator coordinates all aspects of 
this Annex. 
2. This Annex complies with the National Response Framework (NRF), and the National 
Incident Management System (NIMS). The NIMS guides the direction and control 
system adopted by the Navajo County Emergency Management, which functions as the 
official disaster prevention, protection, response, preparedness, recovery, and mitigation 
organization within the Navajo County. 
3. It may operate at two levels: 1.) Navajo County EOC; and 2.) Field operations. 
4. During emergency activations, all management decisions regarding transportation for 
the Navajo County are made at the Navajo County EOC by the coordinator. Under the 
Incident Command System (ICS) structure, the Planning, Logistics, Finance 
& Administration, and Operations Section and associated staff at the Navajo County 
EOC assist the incident commander in carrying out the overall mission. 
5. In accordance with a mission assignment, each primary and/or support organization 
assisting in the deployment of this Annex will retain administrative control over its own 
resources and personnel, but will be under the operational control of this Annex. Mission 
operational control may be delegated to the field by the Navajo County EOC. 
C. Organization

<!-- page 968 -->
818  
1. County  
1. During an activation of the Navajo County EOC, primary and support agency 
staff are integrated with the FBI Pinetop-Lakeside / Navajo County Emergency 
Management / Navajo County Information Technology / Navajo County Sheriff's 
Office staff to provide support. 
2. During an emergency or disaster event, the Navajo County EOC, Operations 
Section Chief will coordinate resource support with the Infrastructure Services 
Branch Chief. 
3. During the response phase, the Navajo County EOC will evaluate and analyze 
information regarding transportation services requests. This Annex will develop 
and update assessments of the transportation services status in the impacted 
area and undertake contingency planning to meet anticipated transportation 
requirements. 
4. The FBI Pinetop-Lakeside / Navajo County Emergency Management / Navajo 
County Information Technology / Navajo County Sheriff's Office will develop and 
maintain the Annex and accompanying Appendices, Annexes and Standard 
Operating Guidelines that govern response actions related to emergencies. 
Primary and support agencies should develop and maintain their own similar 
documents for internal use, which must be compatible with and in support of the 
overall EOP. All such documents will be in compliance with the National 
Response Framework (NRF), The National Incident Management System 
(NIMS), the Incident Command System (ICS), and the Navajo County EOP. 
5. The FBI Pinetop-Lakeside / Navajo County Emergency Management / Navajo 
County Information Technology / Navajo County Sheriff's Office shall be 
represented in the Annex most pertinent to the support of disaster intelligence 
collection and scope of response. 
2. State of Arizona   
1. During an emergency or disaster event, the primary and support agencies at the 
will report to the Infrastructure Services Branch Chief, who reports to the 
Operations Section Chief under the overall direction of the State Emergency 
Operations Center (SEOC) Manager. 
2. The Arizona Department of Homeland Security & Emergency Management, 
reviews and maintains the overall actions of this Annex. Primary and support 
agencies should develop and maintain their own similar documents for internal 
use, which must be compatible with and in support of the overall Arizona 
Response Plan. All such documents will be in compliance with the National 
Response Framework (NRF), the National Incident Management System (NIMS), 
the Incident Command System (ICS) and the Arizona Response Plan.

1. The FBI Pinetop-Lakeside / Navajo County Emergency Management / Navajo County 
Information Technology / Navajo County Sheriff's Office will notify the County Warning

Point (Navajo County Governmental Complex) when information comes to their attention 
indicating that an emergency or disaster situation is developing. 
2. The County Warning Point (Navajo County Governmental Complex), will notify the on-
call Emergency Duty Officer or the Coordinator when Navajo County has been 
threatened or impacted by an emergency or disaster event as provided in the County 
Warning Point procedure. 
3. This Annex will be activated or placed on standby upon notification by the Navajo 
County EOC. The representatives or designees of the coordinating agency will manage 
the emergency activities. If additional support is required, the coordinating and primary 
agencies may jointly manage activities. 
4. Upon instructions to activate or place staff on standby, FBI Pinetop-Lakeside / Navajo 
County Emergency Management / Navajo County Information Technology / Navajo 
County Sheriff's Office will implement procedures to notify all planning team members 
and, if necessary, mobilize all personnel, facilities and physical resources likely to be 
needed, based on the emergency circumstance.

Response, Recovery and Mitigation. Actions specifically designated for Vulnerable 
Needs populations are listed separately in conjunction with the Annex actions. Each 
phase requires specific skills and knowledge to accomplish the tasks and requires 
significant cooperation and collaboration between all agencies and the intended 
recipients of service.

No Responsibilities have been assigned. 
IV. Financial Management 
 
A. This Annex is responsible for coordinating with Navajo County Finance Department to 
manage expenses relevant to an event. 
 
B. During a response, each agency/department fund disaster operations from their current 
operating budget and are responsible for recording and tracking agency expenditures. If a 
federally declared disaster exists, each agency is responsible for seeking reimbursement in 
accordance to the formula established by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) 
via the FEMA-State Agreement. 
 
C. Expenditures by support entities will be documented by those entities and submitted directly 
to the Navajo County Finance Department or a designated Finance Service officer as soon as 
possible. 
V. References and Authorities 
 
REFERENCES 
1. Comprehensive Preparedness Guidance (CPG) 101, Developing and Maintaining 
Emergency Operations Plans, Version 3.0, September 2021. 
 
AUTHORITIES 
1. 44 CFR Part 13 - Uniform Administrative Requirements for Grants and Cooperative 
Agreements. 
2. 44 CFR Part 206 - Federal Disaster Assistance for Disasters Declared after November 
23, 1988. 
 
If Federal agencies become involved with any assistance during a disaster or emergency, 
a Presidential declared disaster is generally required which will be requested by the 
governor's office through the Cabinet Secretary of the Department of Homeland Security 
& Emergency Management. To understand this process more, it is described within 
FEMA Publication P-682 National Response Framework and FEMA Publication P-683. To 
obtain further information on the Federal assistance process and how it is structured you 
can find both of these publications in the File Archive portion of this living plan.

I. Purpose and Scope 
 
A. Purpose  
1. The purpose of this Annex is to provide resources of member agencies to support 
emergency response needs in the Navajo County. 
B. Scope

<!-- page 984 -->
834  
1. This Annex addresses both emergency assistance and the maintenance and mitigation 
efforts for responses specific to this Annex. Specifically, it discusses: 
  
2. Encompassed in this Annex is information on standard operating procedures (SOP), 
movement of responders, victims and supplies associated with response and recover 
efforts following a major disaster, egress and ingress information. Also included is 
information on major services by coordinating agencies critical to the welfare of the 
citizens of the Navajo County. 
II. Concept of Operations 
 
A. General  
1. This Annex is consistent with the Navajo County EOC's methodology, the requirements 
of the National Response Framework (NRF), the National Incident Management System 
(NIMS), and the Incident Command System (ICS). This structure and system supports 
incident assessment, planning, procurement, deployment, and coordination and support 
operations to the Navajo County through the Navajo County Emergency Policy Group, 
Area Operations and Regional Incident Management Teams (IMT) to provide a timely 
and appropriate response to an emergency or situation. 
2. Procedures, protocols and plans for disaster response activities are to govern staff 
operations at the Navajo County EOC and in the field. These are in the form of the base 
plan and corresponding Appendices, ESF Annexes, Support Annexes, Threat 
Annexes, and Standard Operating Guidelines, which describe capabilities. Periodic 
training and exercises are also conducted to enhance effectiveness. 
3. In a large event requiring local or State mutual aid assistance, Annex will work with its 
support agency counterparts to seek and procure, plan, coordinate or direct the use of 
required assets. 
4. Throughout the response and recovery periods, these agencies will evaluate and 
analyze information requests to move people, materials, equipment and other resources 
as necessary. 
B. Direction and Control  
1. The Coordinating Agency is Navajo County Emergency Management / Navajo County 
Public Health Services District / White Mountain Apache Tribe Health Authority which is 
approved by the Arizona Department of Emergency and Military Affairs Cabinet 
Secretary, in coordination with local planning partners. The staff member serving as the 
Coordinator is appointed by and located in the Navajo County Emergency Management / 
Navajo County Public Health Services District / White Mountain Apache Tribe Health 
Authority. When support is necessary, the Coordinator coordinates all aspects of this 
Annex. 
2. This Annex complies with the National Response Framework (NRF), and the National 
Incident Management System (NIMS). The NIMS guides the direction and control 
system adopted by the Navajo County Emergency Management, which functions as the

<!-- page 985 -->
835  
official disaster prevention, protection, response, preparedness, recovery, and mitigation 
organization within the Navajo County. 
3. It may operate at two levels: 1.) Navajo County EOC; and 2.) Field operations. 
4. During emergency activations, all management decisions regarding transportation for 
the Navajo County are made at the Navajo County EOC by the coordinator. Under the 
Incident Command System (ICS) structure, the Planning, Logistics, Finance 
& Administration, and Operations Section and associated staff at the Navajo County 
EOC assist the incident commander in carrying out the overall mission. 
5. In accordance with a mission assignment, each primary and/or support organization 
assisting in the deployment of this Annex will retain administrative control over its own 
resources and personnel, but will be under the operational control of this Annex. Mission 
operational control may be delegated to the field by the Navajo County EOC. 
C. Organization  
1. County  
1. During an activation of the Navajo County EOC, primary and support agency 
staff are integrated with the Navajo County Emergency Management / Navajo 
County Public Health Services District / White Mountain Apache Tribe Health 
Authority staff to provide support. 
2. During an emergency or disaster event, the Navajo County EOC, Operations 
Section Chief will coordinate resource support with the Infrastructure Services 
Branch Chief. 
3. During the response phase, the Navajo County EOC will evaluate and analyze 
information regarding transportation services requests. This Annex will develop 
and update assessments of the transportation services status in the impacted 
area and undertake contingency planning to meet anticipated transportation 
requirements. 
4. The Navajo County Emergency Management / Navajo County Public Health 
Services District / White Mountain Apache Tribe Health Authority will develop and 
maintain the Annex and accompanying Appendices, Annexes and Standard 
Operating Guidelines that govern response actions related to emergencies. 
Primary and support agencies should develop and maintain their own similar 
documents for internal use, which must be compatible with and in support of the 
overall EOP. All such documents will be in compliance with the National 
Response Framework (NRF), The National Incident Management System 
(NIMS), the Incident Command System (ICS), and the Navajo County EOP. 
5. The Navajo County Emergency Management / Navajo County Public Health 
Services District / White Mountain Apache Tribe Health Authority shall be 
represented in the Annex most pertinent to the support of disaster intelligence 
collection and scope of response. 
2. State of Arizona

<!-- page 986 -->
836  
1. During an emergency or disaster event, the primary and support agencies at the 
will report to the Infrastructure Services Branch Chief, who reports to the 
Operations Section Chief under the overall direction of the State Emergency 
Operations Center (SEOC) Manager. 
2. The Arizona Department of Homeland Security & Emergency Management, 
reviews and maintains the overall actions of this Annex. Primary and support 
agencies should develop and maintain their own similar documents for internal 
use, which must be compatible with and in support of the overall Arizona 
Response Plan. All such documents will be in compliance with the National 
Response Framework (NRF), the National Incident Management System (NIMS), 
the Incident Command System (ICS) and the Arizona Response Plan. 
D. Alerts and Notifications  
1. The Navajo County Emergency Management / Navajo County Public Health Services 
District / White Mountain Apache Tribe Health Authority will notify the County Warning 
Point (Navajo County Governmental Complex) when information comes to their attention 
indicating that an emergency or disaster situation is developing. 
2. The County Warning Point (Navajo County Governmental Complex), will notify the on-
call Emergency Duty Officer or the Coordinator when Navajo County has been 
threatened or impacted by an emergency or disaster event as provided in the County 
Warning Point procedure. 
3. This Annex will be activated or placed on standby upon notification by the Navajo 
County EOC. The representatives or designees of the coordinating agency will manage 
the emergency activities. If additional support is required, the coordinating and primary 
agencies may jointly manage activities. 
4. Upon instructions to activate or place staff on standby, Navajo County Emergency 
Management / Navajo County Public Health Services District / White Mountain Apache 
Tribe Health Authority will implement procedures to notify all planning team members 
and, if necessary, mobilize all personnel, facilities and physical resources likely to be 
needed, based on the emergency circumstance. 
E. Actions  
1. Actions carried out are grouped into phases of emergency management: Preparedness, 
Response, Recovery and Mitigation. Actions specifically designated for Vulnerable 
Needs populations are listed separately in conjunction with the Annex actions. Each 
phase requires specific skills and knowledge to accomplish the tasks and requires 
significant cooperation and collaboration between all agencies and the intended 
recipients of service.

The following list identifies the responsibilities designated to each of the Primary and Support 
Agencies for this Emergency Support Function. The Primary Agency and its responsibilities are 
listed first. The Supporting Agencies follow in alphabetical order.

Preparedness (Pre-Event) Actions for Threat Annex G - Pandemic 
1 Maintain a personnel roster, contact, and resource lists. 
2 Anticipate health and medical requirements for AFN populations. 
3 Ensure adequate EMS coverage throughout the planning area. 
4 Identify alternate or backup facilities for daily functions of Public Health and Medical 
Services. 
5 Determine the availability of resources for hospital facilities, staff, EMS, volunteers, and 
outside assistance. 
6 Identify fatality management capabilities. 
7 Have working plans for patient transport to all sites, including overflow and out of area. 
8 Designate alternative sites, extra jurisdictional if needed, for patient capacity exceeding 
capabilities. 
9 Maintain current MOUs or MOAs. 
10 Identify liaisons to communicate with local health department, Points of Dispensing, 
hospitals and the state health department. 
11 Participate in county-wide medical countermeasure planning. 
12 Plan for quarantine and containment activities. 
13 Evaluate the EOCs ability to respond to disasters longer than 24 hours. 
14 Have a clear press release and mass media protocol for communication to the public 
during emergencies. 
15 Participate in the CDC Public Health Preparedness Program. 
16 Collaborate with Department of Agriculture, Health and Human Services, CDC, FDA, and 
related organizations on programs tracking potential pandemics and epidemics. 
17 Plan for decontamination activities. 
18 Create/review EAP protocols as appropriate 
19 Identify alternate EOC locations and requirements to activate. 
20 Coordinate and participate in training, drills, and exercises; including position specific 
training for EOC operations. 
21 Identify who is responsible for initial notification of EOC personnel. 
22 Identify responsibilities for liaison roles with state and adjacent county emergency 
management officials. 
23 Prepare for inter-agency cooperation by practicing response coordination with health 
departments in a health crisis requiring mass care. 
24 Coordinate health departments' emergency response training programs. 
Response (During Event) Actions for Threat Annex G - Pandemic 
1 Anticipate health and medical requirements for AFN populations. 
2 Identify alternate or backup facilities for daily functions of Public Health and Medical 
Services. 
3 Determine the availability of resources for hospital facilities, staff, EMS, volunteers, and 
outside assistance. 
4 Designate alternative sites, extra jurisdictional if needed, for patient capacity exceeding 
capabilities. 
5 Collect, process, and disseminate information to and from the EOC.

7 Coordinate community medication dispensing activities.

9 
For help providing mass medical care and treating displaced populations, coordinate with 
the Red Cross and other charities including Salvation Army; designate personnel as 
liaisons. 
10 Upon identification of medical resource shortfalls activate warehousing operations. 
11 Support the preparation of Incident Action Plans (IAP) and distribute to appropriate 
partners. 
12 Identify any needed specialized resources that are unavailable to responding entities. 
13 Determine the nature and scope of the disaster or incident by consulting with the EM 
Director.

IV. Financial Management 
 
A. This Annex is responsible for coordinating with Navajo County Finance Department to 
manage expenses relevant to an event. 
 
B. During a response, each agency/department fund disaster operations from their current 
operating budget and are responsible for recording and tracking agency expenditures. If a 
federally declared disaster exists, each agency is responsible for seeking reimbursement in 
accordance to the formula established by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) 
via the FEMA-State Agreement. 
 
C. Expenditures by support entities will be documented by those entities and submitted directly 
to the Navajo County Finance Department or a designated Finance Service officer as soon as 
possible. 
V. References and Authorities 
 
REFERENCES 
1. Comprehensive Preparedness Guidance (CPG) 101, Developing and Maintaining 
Emergency Operations Plans, Version 3.0, September 2021.

<!-- page 1014 -->
864  
AUTHORITIES 
1. 44 CFR Part 13 - Uniform Administrative Requirements for Grants and Cooperative 
Agreements. 
2. 44 CFR Part 206 - Federal Disaster Assistance for Disasters Declared after November 
23, 1988. 
 
If Federal agencies become involved with any assistance during a disaster or emergency, 
a Presidential declared disaster is generally required which will be requested by the 
governor's office through the Cabinet Secretary of the Department of Homeland Security 
& Emergency Management. To understand this process more, it is described within 
FEMA Publication P-682 National Response Framework and FEMA Publication P-683. To 
obtain further information on the Federal assistance process and how it is structured you 
can find both of these publications in the File Archive portion of this living plan.
