5A) CLOUD /S AA S VS . ON-PREM DISCOVERY & ARCHITECTURE STRATEGY  
The County’s next decision is not only which  platform to use, but where  to run it. Convergint 
recommends an upfront Cloud Readiness & Architecture Discovery  to weigh the benefits of 
cloud/SaaS , on-premises , and hybrid  designs—measured against Navajo County’s support 
capacity, network realities, resiliency goals, and total cost of ownership. 
Scope of the discovery.  Workshops with Sheriff, Facilities, and IT map use -cases, SLAs, and 
constraints; inventory compute/storage; and documen t bandwidth, site connectivity, and failover 
expectations. We then compare deployment models : 
• On-Prem / Virtualized:  maximum local control and predictable performance for 
high-bitrate recording; leverages County data center; requires patching/backup discipline. 
• Cloud / SaaS:  rapid deployment, simplified patching, elastic storage; depends on reliable 
WAN; attention to egress costs, retention economics, and data residency. 
• Hybrid:  cloud-managed with edge appliances  for local recording/offline resilience; 
centralized policy with distributed enforcement—often ideal for detention/justice. 
Evaluation dimensions.  Resiliency (RTO/RPO), cybersecurity, degraded-mode  behavior, 
latency/bandwidth, lifecycle and patch cadence, data residency/retention, identity/SSO integration, 
staffing/support, and five-year cost  (CapEx/OpEx). 
Vendor roadmaps & fit.  Major ecosystems (Genetec, LenelS2, Milestone, Avi gilon/Motorola, 
Genea Solutions) have different SaaS/hybrid maturit y. Convergint translates each roadmap into 
County-specific pros/cons so the decision is manufacturer-agnostic. 
Leverage County cloud.  If the County already has AWS or Azure , Convergint can reuse those 
investments—hosting components in your tenancy, integrating Entra ID/SSO/MFA , using object 
storage tiers for video archives, and applying your governance/backup policies. 
Deliverables.  A Cloud Decision Brief  with recommended architecture (on-prem, SaaS, or 
hybrid), security/identity plan (SSO/MFA, SCIM/LDAP ), retention economics, and a phased 
migration roadmap. Where useful, we stand up a cloud pilot  in parallel with the sandbox to 
validate performance and user experience before scale-out.

5D) OPEN , NON -PROPRIETARY DETENTION CONTROLS (PLC-BASED ) 
Detention controls should be open, serviceable, and future-proof —not gated by a single 
proprietary vendor. Convergint recommends industrial PLC-based  detention systems with open 
programming  and commercial off-the-shelf (COTS)  components to protect the County’s 
investment and keep competition healthy over time. 
Why PLC-based and open?  
• Flexibility & scalability:  Standard I/O, modular racks, and open logic scale from a single 
pod to an entire complex. 
• Serviceability:  Multiple qualified firms can maintain hardware and  logic; spare parts are 
broadly available. 
• Longevity:  Industrial lifecycles and roadmap continuity reduc e forklift upgrades and 
vendor lock-in. 
• Transparency:  Documented logic, naming, and HMI standards make o perations 
understandable to County staff. 
Reference architecture.  
• Core control:  Redundant PLCs for door control, interlocks, sally  ports, lights/calls, and 
emergency overrides. 
• HMI/SCADA:  Modern operator stations with clear mimic panels, activity logs, and alarm 
acknowledgements. 
• Integration points:  
o Access control (ACS):  Share door status/commands via secure gateways or 
discrete I/O as policy dictates. 
o Video (VMS):  Trigger call-ups/recording boosts on interlocks, duress, or cell-door 
events; stamp events in audit logs. 
o Intercom/duress:  Event-driven workflows to operator consoles with r ecorded 
audio and call trees.

6.1 Governance & Standards 
• Frameworks.  We map controls to County policy using NIST CSF / CIS Controls ; 
where applicable, we respect CJIS  considerations for admin access, workstation posture, 
and log retention. 
• Change control.  All changes (firmware, configuration, credentials) are tracked in 
iCare™ with approvals, scheduling, and rollback plans; device-level acceptance is 
captured in iTrac™. 
• Segregation of duties.  Admin roles for ACS, VMS, weapons detection, and detention 
controls are separated; privileged activities require named accounts and just-in-time 
elevation where supported. 
6.2 Identity, Access & Authentication 
• SSO/MFA.  Administrative consoles (ACS/VMS/analytics) integrate with County Entra 
ID/AD  via SAML/OIDC ; MFA is enforced for privileged roles. 
• RBAC.  Fine-grained roles limit what each admin can see and change; operator roles are 
task-based (monitoring, evidence export, credential changes). 
• Privileged secrets.  Break-glass and service accounts are stored in the County’s 
PAM/secret vault  (e.g., Key Vault) with check-out/check-in  and audit. 
6.3 Network Architecture & Segmentation 
• Zones.  Separate camera/IoT VLANs , ACS/PLC control VLANs , and management  
networks with ACLs; restrict east-west and block internet egress unless explicitly 
required. 
• 802.1X/NAC.  Use 802.1X  (or MAB where needed) on access ports; deny unknown 
MACs by default. 
• Time & trust.  NTP synchronization; management over TLS 1.2+ / HTTPS ; disable 
insecure services (telnet, HTTP, anonymous SNMP). Readers use OSDP Secure 
Channel . 
6.4 Device Hardening & Credential Hygiene (All IoT, incl. Access Panels) 
• Baseline build.  Remove/disable default accounts; rotate or vault all local admin 
passwords; enforce complexity and lockouts; unique creds per device class. 
• Password rotation policy.  
o Admin/root on devices:  rotate 90–180 days  (risk-based). 
o Service/integration accounts:  rotate 90 days ; vault and inject where supported. 
o OSDP SC keys:  rotate annually  or on staff/vendor change. 
o Certificates:  use X.509 for cameras/servers; ≤12-month  validity with auto-renew 
where possible. 
• Configuration lock-down.  Disable unused protocols/ports, set least-privilege SNMPv3, 
restrict remote shell, and apply signed firmware only. 
6.5 Patch, Firmware & Vulnerability Management

7) CHANGE MANAGEMENT & ADOPTION PLAN  
Modernization succeeds when people adopt the new wa y of working before  the last device is 
commissioned. Convergint treats change management a s a workstream with its own scope, 
schedule, and outcomes—not a training class at the end. 
We start with early, role-based training —short, task-focused sessions scheduled before the first 
production cutover. Operators learn maps, alarm han dling, weapons-detection SOPs  (where 
deployed), and incident workflows; administrators p ractice credential lifecycle, permissions, 
reporting, and PLC/HMI  role basics where detention controls are in scope;  County technicians 
learn the top fixes that prevent avoidable truck ro lls. Materials, recordings, and quick-reference 
guides are posted in iCare™ for easy access and future onboarding. To make pra ctice safe and 
realistic, we stand up a sandbox (test/development) environment  that mirrors the County’s 
configuration: sites, devices, roles, maps, and (wh ere applicable) simulated detectors—seeded 
with sanitized/synthetic data—so staff can practice without risk. 
Because identity data is the backbone of access con trol, we treat database cleanup  as a 
mini-project: deduplicate cardholders, normalize fo rmats and facility codes, collapse redundant 
access levels into roles, and stage imports through  the sandbox. We then manage badging 
migration  explicitly—dual-technology HID Signo or Wavelynx  readers allow legacy and new 
credentials to coexist; re-badging events are scheduled by department; mobile credentials  can be 
piloted with MDM safeguards. To keep the database c lean after go-live, we implement HR and 
Active Directory integrations —daily HR feeds as the authoritative source, AD/Ent ra groups 
mapped to access roles, SSO for administrators, and  monthly reconciliations to catch drift. We 
acknowledge the human change curve  and run a 30/60/90-day hyper-care  program with 
floor-walking in week one, a staffed support bridge , weekly adoption check-ins, and metrics that 
show progress.

screening , the County gains a dependable, auditable capability that endures. Our service models  
and Grants & Funding Team , combined with our ~$500M annual SLED depth , give Navajo 
County practical options for timely support, extern al financing, and confidence that the program 
aligns with proven public-sector best practices. 
 
 
19) PRE CONSTRUCTION COST PROPOSAL  
 
Convergint is providing a cost proposal to meet the following scope of work as it relates to preconstruction, 
discovery, ESMR and estimating 
 
- Convergint proposes to walk the County through a fu ll ESRM as well as Stakholder 
Investigation and detailed estimating phases. This includes the following: 
 On site, in person meetings with all Stakeholders to identify and build a clear path 
forward for the forseesable future (5 year roadmap) 
 Follow up and subsequent meetings will be via Teams where appropriate 
 Investigation and surveys of each of the County’s sites in person. 
 Provide interviews with product partners who align with the County’s long term 
goals (most likely in Teams but may be in person) 
 Help the County decide what technologies meet your best interests. 
 Provide cost estimates for each building and/or phases.

Board of Supervisors Regular 8. a.        
Meeting Date: 01/27/2026  
Title: SUP 25-004 Winding Canyon Wind - MET Tower, District III
Submitted For: Katherine Wright, Planner II  Submitted By: Katherine Wright, Planner II
Department: Planning & Development Services 
Presented By: Katherine Wright
Motion before the Board:
Consideration and adoption of Resolution Number 01-2026, approving/denying a Special Use Permit for
the construction and operation of one meteorological monitoring tower (MET tower) on approximately
.7479 acres of vacant land southwest of Joseph City. 
Background:
APN#: 111-07-003A, T16N, R17E, S05, 07, 09, 17 of the GSRM.  Owner: Aztec Land & Cattle
Company, Ltd.  Agent: Kevin Gooley.
February 29, 2024 – Arizona Game and Fish Department (AZGFD) reviewed the proposed installation of
the MET tower and provided comments.
April 20, 2024 – Arizona Game and Fish Department (AZGFD) clarified with the applicant that
participation in the Motus program is an optional opportunity.  The applicant will continue to work with
AZGFD through the development of the project and explore the implementation of the Motus telemetry
tracking station.
August 25, 2025 – The MET tower filing was submitted to the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA).
The actual MET tower will be on .7479 acres; however, the full parcel of land is 2,761.22 acres.  The
proposed MET tower will collect meteorological data to inform the energy assessment of a future
potential wind energy generation facility. 
The MET tower will be 272 feet tall.  It will be a tubular tilt-up tower with guy wires, including a
1-2-meter (3.28-6.56-foot) lightning rod.  The smallest of the setbacks is 1,667.97 feet from property lines
and well above the minimum tower setback requirement for non-residential setbacks of 1:1 foot.
Subject to FAA’s sign off and Navajo County’s approval, the installation of the MET tower will occur
within a few months after receiving the SUP and Building Permit.  If approved, the MET tower will be
installed shortly thereafter.  The installation will take 1 to 3 days to complete.  The MET tower is
expected to operate for up to seven (7) years.
The MET tower will be accessed from the intersection of State Route 99 and Territorial Road.  After
approximately 8.3 miles from the intersection, access goes south on the County Maintained section of
Bell Cow Road for approximately 1.5 miles when Bell Cow Road turns into a private road, with site
access granted via sub easement licenses with private landowners.

Navajo County Planning & Development Services Staff recommend approval of the Special Use Permit,

SPECIAL USE PERMIT 
 APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS 
 
In applying for a SPECIAL USE PERMIT, the following is required of all applications: 
 
1. Special Use Permit application  (completed). All information requested on the 
application shall be complete, including ownership (which shall be legally notarized 
where indicated).  
 
2. A copy of the recorded deed or sales contract. 
 
3. Site Plan, as noted below: 
 
▪ 2 (two) copies of the site plan at 24” x 36” – folded to approximately 9” x 12” 
▪ 2 (two) copies of the site plan at 8-½” x 11” 
▪ Note that after initial review, staff may require additional copies, a different scale, 
and/or different paper sizes 
▪ Additional copies of the site plan and other application materials may be 
required prior to the Planning Commission and/or Board of Supervisors 
meetings 
 
 The site plan shall be drawn to a 50, 100, or 200 foot -to-the-inch scale, or an 
alternate scale if approve d by the Planning Director and /or County Engineer, 
whichever is most appropriate to clearly present necessary details. At a minimum, 
the site plan shall include the following: 
 
▪ Project name / title 
▪ North arrow and scale 
▪ Property lines with dimensions 
▪ Location and dimensions of all existing or proposed structures 
▪ Distances from structures to property lines, septic, and water well facilities 
▪ All required yard setbacks from property lines and distances between buildings 
▪ All existing and proposed ingress and egress (access) for the subject property, 
including the widths of all driveways 
▪ Adjacent street names and right-of-way widths 
▪ All interior drive and parking area s (including any handicapped -accessible 
parking). Include the proposed surfacing for these areas 
▪ Site data table, which is to include the following: 
- Site size in acres 
- Address of the site 
-  Assessor’s Parcel Number(s) of the site 
- General Legal Description of the property (Township, Range and Section). If 
located within a platted subdivision, provide the subdivision name, lot 
number(s) and recording information (Book & Page) 
-  Existing zoning of the site 
-  Existing and proposed use(s) 
-  Size & details for any proposed structures (type, size in square feet, height, 
etc.) 
-  Parking (where needed) – indicate the number of spaces – both proposed &

required (include handicapped-accessible spaces) 
- Service providers – table format (water, method of sewage disposal, trash, fire, 
police, electric, gas, etc.). Note that “will serve” letters may be required 
- Contact information (name, address, phone & e-mail) for the owner, developer, 
architect/engineer, owner’s representative and/or other persons 
▪ Details and locations regarding proposed fencing/screening & signs 
▪ Adjacent land uses, parcel numbers and ownership name

4. A “Project Narrative” (2 copies), expressing your reasons for the proposed Special

5. A “Vicinity Map” (2 copies), including a written and graphic description of how to

Longitude of the “corners” of the site. 
 
6. The correct Application Fee (see fee schedule) – payable to Navajo County. 
 
7. Additional Materials (optional – not required). A CD (Compact Disk) of a copy of all

additional materials may also be submitted to better explain the proposed 
development. Although not required, these may include aerial photos, context plans, 
building elevations, landscape plans, letters of support, renderings, sign details, etc. 
 
All application materials and other required information concerning a Special Use Permit 
must be submitted to the Planning & Zoning Division of the Public Works Department for 
review and staff approval prior to scheduling of any hearings before the Planning & Zoning 
Commission and/or the Board of Supervisors. The Planning & Zoning Commission meets 
the third Thursday of each month (6:00 p.m.), and the Board of Supervisors meets the 
second and fourth Tuesday’s of each month (9:00 a.m.) All hearings are held in the Board 
of Supervisors’ C hambers at the Navajo County Governmental Center in Holbrook, 
Arizona. Please confirm any hearings with staff, as dates, times and locations may change.

I. Introduction 
Winding Canyon Wind Farm, LLC (Applicant) respectfully requests a Special Use Permit (SUP) from 
Navajo County for the construction and operation of one meteorological monitoring tower (MET tower). 
The proposed MET tower location would be located on one privately owned parcel located approximately 
20.19 miles southwest of Joseph City, Arizona. The parcel is privately owned by Aztec Land and Cattle 
Company, Ltd.  
If approved, the MET tower will collect meteorological data to inform the energy assessment of a future 
potential wind energy generation facility (Winding Canyon Wind Farm).  
Attachment 1 includes the Application Form, which is notarized by the landowner, Aztec Land & Cattle 
Co Ltd. 
Winding Canyon Wind Farm LLC is a wholly owned subsidiary of EDP Renewables North America LLC 
(EDPR NA). EDPR NA. its affiliates, and subsidiaries develop, construct, own, and operate wind farms, 
solar parks, and energy storage systems throughout North America. Headquartered in Houston, Texas, 
with 61 wind farms, 26 solar parks, and eight regional offices across North America, EDPR NA has 
developed more than 12,000 megawatts (MW) and operates more than 11,400 MW of onshore utility-
scale renewable energy projects. 
EDPR NA conducts most of its business in rural communities across the U.S., Canada, and Mexico. 
Obtaining and maintaining credibility and the trust of landowners, town officials, and other stakeholders 
is a crucial aspect of building successful projects. At EDPR NA, our community relationships represent 
more than business transactions. We value strong relationships with landowners and communities who 
see the possibilities of conscientious land stewardship, rural economic development, and contributing to a 
more sustainable future.  
II. Project Overview 
Winding Canyon Wind Farm LLC proposes to locate the MET tower approximately 20.19 miles 
southwest of Joseph City, Arizona. The MET tower will be located on parcel number 111-07-003A, 
which is owned by Aztec Land & Cattle Co Ltd (Table 1). The MET tower will be 83 meters (272 feet) 
tall. It will be a tubular tilt-up tower with guy wires, including a 1–2-meter lightening rod. 
 
Attachment 2 includes a copy of the recorded memorandum of the land agreement between EDP 
Renewables North America LLC, and Aztec Land & Cattle Co Ltd. The landowner is grazing cattle on 
this privately owned land and will continue to do so in conjunction with the operations of this proposed 
MET tower.

Attachment 3 includes the proposed project Site Plan, demonstrating the location of the development.  
This land is zoned as A-General which is a designation for all the unincorporated area of the County, 
except land within the boundary of a reservation and outside the authority of Navajo County. Uses 
permitted in the "A-General Zone" include farm and non-farm residential uses, farms, recreational, 
institutional, commercial, and industrial uses as specifically listed in this Article. Other uses may be 
permitted as Special Uses under Article 20.  
According to the Navajo County zoning ordinance, the MET tower will require a Special Use designation 
as it does not qualify for the uses permitted in the “A-General Zone.” 
On August 25, 2025, the MET tower filing was submitted to the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA). 
The ASN is 2025-WTW-11628-OE. See Attachment 4 for the confirmation of filing.  
On February 29, 2024, Arizona Game and Fish Department (AZGFD) reviewed the proposed installation 
of the MET tower and provided comments. On April 20, 2024, AZGFD clarified with the Applicant that 
participation in the Motus program is an optional opportunity. The Applicant will continue to work with 
AZGFD through the development of the project and explore the implementation of the Motus telemetry 
tracking station. See Attachment 5 for the referenced letter from AZGFD. 
III. Schedule for MET tower Development 
Subject to FAA’s sign off and Navajo County’s approval, the installation of the MET tower will occur 
within a few months after receiving the SUP and building permit. If approved, the MET tower will be 
installed shortly thereafter. The installation will take 1 to 3 days to complete. The MET tower is expected 
to operate for up to seven years. 
The nearest State Highway is State Route 377, and the closest Federal Road is Interstate 40.  
The MET tower will be accessed from the intersection of State Route 99 and Territorial Road. After 
approximately 8.3 miles from the intersection, access goes south on the County Maintained section of 
Bell Cow Road for approximately 1.5 miles when Bell Cow Road turns into a private road, with site 
access granted via sub easement licenses with private landowners.  
Attachment 6 includes a copy of the proposed Vicinity Map, including proposed access points. 
Attachment 7 includes a schematic of the proposed MET tower. 
IV. Benefits to Navajo County 
The proposed MET tower will collect meteorological data to inform the energy assessment of a future 
potential wind energy generation facility. If developed, the future wind project will be beneficial to 
Navajo County by providing family-wage jobs and economic growth to the local community. There will 
be additional tax revenue from the potential wind farm that can benefit the local community.

<!-- page 1254 -->
V. Compatibility of Proposed Use with Adjacent Uses and 
Character of the Area 
The proposed MET tower is compatible with adjacent uses and the character of the area. The proposed 
MET tower complies with Navajo County’s Comprehensive Plan, including the identified Character 
Areas Map, and the Aztec Area Plan. This is demonstrated by reviewing the following documents from 
Navajo County: 
1. Navajo County Comprehensive Plan 
a. Character Areas Map – Range Land 
The proposed MET tower will be in the character area designated as Range Land. The Range 
Land character area is designated for lands that are large private tracts or other property that 
is, and likely will continue to be, used for ranching purposes. 
The development of a MET tower in this character area will not hinder the ability of the land 
to be used for agricultural purposes. The landowner plans to continue cattle grazing activities 
on the land during the operations of the met tower and operational life of the prospective 
wind farm. 
b. Aztec Area Plan 
The proposed MET tower project complies with the Aztec Area Plan, which serves as a guide 
for future development of a 228,040-acre property (about 356 square miles) property owned 
by Aztec Land and Cattle Company, Limited (Aztec, Ltd.), Aztec Land Company, LLC 
(Aztec, LLC) and Aztec Despain Ranch LLC. The Navajo County Comprehensive Plan 
Section 1.6 supports the Aztec Area Plan as a community plan to assess future development 
on private lands in unincorporated Navajo County. The proposed MET tower is within the 
property boundaries of the Aztec Area plan that are suitable for future wind energy 
generation development. 
2. Adjacent Uses 
a. The surrounding properties are a combination of Arizona Land Trust and private land 
owned by participating landowners such as Aztec Land & Cattle Co. Limited, McCauley 
Ranch LLC, and Le Soleil Land & Cattle Incorporated.  There is one Federal BLM parcel 
located approximately 2.7 miles from the MET Tower on the western border of the 
project boundary. There are only two legal residences about 1 mile from the closest 
project boundary and about 3 miles from the proposed MET tower. The surrounding area 
consists of predominately agricultural land and ranching.  
b. Since adjacent land use consists of AZ State Land, project participants, and wind farm 
facilities, we believe the proposed MET tower location is compatible with adjacent uses.

October 1st, 2025 
 
Dear Planning Director,  
This is a formal letter to request a waiver from the Neighborhood Community Meeting for a 
Special Use Permit to install a meteorological tower for surveying wind potential at our 
Winding Canyon Wind Farm , per the guidance provided in  Section 2907 – Citizen Review, 
Article 29 of the Navajo County Zoning Ordinance. 
The meteorological tower will be 272 feet tall, located at 110 32’ 59’ W / 34 47’ 49’ N in Sec 
9 16N 17E, parcel number 111-07-003A. The surrounding land parcels are owned by either 
project participants or the Arizona State Land Department. Project participants are Aztec 
Land & Cattle, McCauley Ranch LLC, and Le Soleil Land and Cattle Inc.  The nearest non -
participating parcel from the Met Tower location is  approximately 8,600 ft (1.6 miles), well 
outside of the required 300’ required for notice (Exhibit A).  
In lieu of a Neighborhood Community Meeting, we will share a public email address for  
citizens to express concerns, problems, or issues with the proposed Special Use. All entries 
from citizens will be documented and shared with the county. 
Because of th e location, it is impractical to host a Neighborhood Community Meeting due 
to proximity to non-participating residents in the area and  we request a waiver from the 
Neighborhood Community Meeting for this Special Use Permit.

ABOUT EDP RENEWABLES
NORTH AMERICA
EDP Renewables North America LLC (EDPR NA), its affiliates, and its subsidiaries develop, 
construct, own, and operate wind farms, solar parks, and energy storage systems throughout North 
America. Headquartered in Houston, Texas, with 60 wind farms, 27 solar parks, and eight regional 
offices across North America, EDPR NA has developed more than 12,000 megawatts (MW) and 
operates more than 11,600 MW of onshore utility-scale renewable energy projects. With more 
than 1,000 employees, EDPR NA’s highly qualified team has a proven capacity to execute projects 
across the continent. 
EDPR NA is a wholly owned subsidiary of EDP Renewables (Euronext: EDPR), is a global leader in 
renewable energy development with a presence in four regions including Europe, North America, 
South America and Asia Pacific. We have a sound development portfolio of top-level assets and 
market-leading operating capacity in renewable energies.
Our business encompasses onshore wind, distributed and large-scale solar, offshore wind 
(through a 50/50 joint venture  - Ocean Winds) and complementary technologies to renewables, 
such as hybridization, storage and green hydrogen.
With 16.5GW deployed across multiple technologies and a €12 billion investment plan up to 
2026, we are committed to driving social progress with a particular focus on sustainability and 
integration. Our employee-centered policies have earnt EDPR a listing in the Bloomberg Gender-
Equality Index and led to recognition as Top Employer 2024 across Europe, Singapore, Brazil, 
Colombia and Chile.

** DETERMINATION OF NO HAZARD TO AIR NAVIGATION **
The Federal Aviation Administration has conducted an aeronautical study under the provisions of 49 U.S.C.,
Section 44718 and if applicable Title 14 of the Code of Federal Regulations, part 77, concerning:
Structure: Met Tower (w/WT Farm) WC MET01
County, State: Navajo, Arizona
Collected Point(s):
Label Latitude Longitude SE DET AGL AMSL
WC MET01 34-47-48.97N 110-32-59.04W 5571 Ft 272 Ft 5843 Ft
In accordance with the provisions of 49 USC 44718 and as applicable 10 USC 183A, this aeronautical study
was sent to the Military Aviation and Installation Assurance Clearinghouse established by the Secretary of
Defense for review.  The results of that review resulted in a finding of no risk to national security.
This aeronautical study revealed that the structure does not exceed obstruction standards and would not be a
hazard to air navigation provided the following condition(s), if any, is(are) met:
As a condition to this Determination, the structure is to be marked/lighted in accordance with FAA
Advisory circular 70/7460-1 M Change 1, Obstruction Marking and Lighting, paint/red lights-Chapters
3(Marked),4,5(Red),&15.
Any failure or malfunction that lasts more than thirty (30) minutes and affects a top light or flashing obstruction
light, regardless of its position, should be reported immediately to (877) 487-6867 so a Notice to Airmen
(NOTAM) can be issued. As soon as the normal operation is restored, notify the same number.
It is required that FAA Form 7460-2, Notice of Actual Construction or Alteration, be e-filed any time the
project is abandoned or:
_____ At least 10 days prior to start of construction (7460-2, Part 1)
__X__ Within 5 days after the construction reaches its greatest height (7460-2, Part 2)

While the structure does not constitute a hazard to air navigation, it would be located within or near a military
training area and/or route.
This determination expires on 07/20/2027 unless:
(a) the construction is started (not necessarily completed) and FAA Form 7460-2, Notice of Actual
Construction or Alteration, is received by this office.
(b) extended, revised, or terminated by the issuing office.
NOTE: REQUEST FOR EXTENSION OF THE EFFECTIVE PERIOD OF THIS DETERMINATION MUST
BE E-FILED AT LEAST 15 DAYS PRIOR TO THE EXPIRATION DATE. AFTER RE-EVALUATION
OF CURRENT OPERATIONS IN THE AREA OF THE STRUCTURE TO DETERMINE THAT NO
SIGNIFICANT AERONAUTICAL CHANGES HAVE OCCURRED, YOUR DETERMINATION MAY BE
ELIGIBLE FOR ONE EXTENSION OF THE EFFECTIVE PERIOD.
This determination is based, in part, on the foregoing description which includes specific coordinates and
heights. This determination is valid for coordinates within one (1) second latitude/longitude and up to the
approved AMSL height listed above (provided the AGL height does not exceed 499 feet). If a certified 1A or
2C accuracy survey was required to mitigate an adverse effect, any change in coordinates or increase in height
will require a new certified accuracy survey and may require a new aeronautical study.
If construction or alteration is dismantled or destroyed, you must submit notice to the FAA within 5 days after
the construction or alteration is dismantled or destroyed.
Additional wind turbines or met towers proposed in the future may cause a cumulative effect on the national
airspace system. All information from submission of Supplemental Notice (7460-2 Part 2) will be considered
the final data (including heights) for this structure. Any future construction or alteration, including but not
limited to changes in heights, requires separate notice to the FAA.
Obstruction marking and lighting recommendations for wind turbine farms are based on the scheme for the
entire project. ANY change to the height, location or number of turbines within this project will require a
reanalysis of the marking and lighting recommendation for the entire project. In particular, the removal of
previously planned or built turbines/turbine locations from the project will often result in a change in the
marking/lighting recommendation for other turbines within the project. It is the proponent's responsibility to
contact the FAA to discuss the process for developing a revised obstruction marking and lighting plan should
this occur.
In order to ensure proper conspicuity of turbines at night during construction, all turbines should be lit with
temporary lighting once they reach a height of 200 feet or greater until such time the permanent lighting
configuration is turned on. As the height of the structure continues to increase, the temporary lighting should
be relocated to the uppermost part of the structure. The temporary lighting may be turned off for periods when
they would interfere with construction personnel. If practical, permanent obstruction lights should be installed
and operated at each level as construction progresses. An FAA Type L-810 steady red light fixture shall be
used to light the structure during the construction phase. If power is not available, turbines shall be lit with self-
contained, solar powered LED steady red light fixture that meets the photometric requirements of an FAA Type
L-810 lighting system. The lights should be positioned to ensure that a pilot has an unobstructed view of at least
one light at each level. The use of a NOTAM (D) to not light turbines within a project until the entire project
has been completed is prohibited.

BOARD OF SUPERVISORS 
 
Hearing Date: January 27th, 2026 
Case No:  SUP 25-004 
Action:   Special Use Permit  
Applicant/Owner: Winding Canyon Wind LLC./Aztec Land & Cattle Company, Ltd. 
Project Name: Winding Canyon Wind – MET Tower 
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY 
Recommendation: The Navajo County Planning and Zoning Commission recommends approval of 
the Staff Report, subject to the conditions of this Staff Report.  
 
Location: The property is located 20.19 miles southwest of Joseph City, on APN# 111-07-003A. 
 
Size: One (1) parcel totaling 2,761.22 acres.  
 
Supervisor District: III. 
 
Zoning: A-General. 
 
Property Owners: Aztec Land & Cattle Company, Ltd. 
 
Applicant: Winding Canyon Wind LLC. 
 
Representative: Kevin Gooley of EDP Renewables North America LLC. 
 
REQUEST DESCRIPTION:  
Consideration of a request for a Special Use Permit  for the construction and operation of one (1) 
meteorological monitoring tower (MET tower) on approximately .7479 acres of vacant land southwest 
of the Joseph City area.  APN#: 111-07-003A, T16N, R17E, S05, 07, 09, 17 of the GSRM.  Owner: 
Aztec Land & Cattle Company, Ltd.  Agent: Kevin Gooley. 
 
GENERAL CHARACTER OF NEIGHBORHOOD:  
 
The subject property is located 20.19 miles southwest of Joseph City.  The nearest state highway is State 
Route 377, and the closest federal road is Interstate 40.  The MET tower will be accessed from the 
intersection of State Route 99 and Territorial Road with private access via Bell Cow Road which is a

<!-- page 1308 -->
Board of Supervisors              2 | P a g e  
 
private road.  All land surrounding the property is vacant. 
 
BACKGROUND/HISTORY: 
 
February 29, 2024 – Arizona Game and Fish Department (AZGFD) reviewed the proposed installation 
of the MET tower and provided comments. 
 
April 20, 2024 – Arizona Game and Fish Department (AZGFD) clarified with the applicant that 
participation in the Motus program is an optional opportunity.  The applicant will continue to work 
with AZGFD through the development of the project and explore th e implementation of the Motus 
telemetry tracking station. 
 
August 25, 2025 – The MET tower filing was submitted to the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA). 
 
PROJECT DESCRIPTION:  
 
The actual MET tower will be on .7479 acres; however, the full parcel of land is 2,761.22 acres.  The 
proposed MET tower will collect meteorological data to inform the energy assessment of a future 
potential wind energy generation facility.   
 
The MET tower will be 272 feet tall.  It will be a tubular tilt -up tower with guy wires, including a 1-2-
meter (3.28-6.56-foot) lightning rod.  The smallest of the setbacks is 1,667.97 feet from property lines 
and well above the minimum tower setback requirement for non-residential setbacks of 1:1 foot. 
 
Subject to FAA’s sign off and Navajo County’s approval, the installation of the MET tower will occur 
within a few months after receiving the SUP and Building Permit.  If approved, the MET tower will be 
installed shortly thereafter.  The installation will take 1 to 3 days to complete.  The MET tower is 
expected to operate for up to seven (7) years. 
 
The MET tower will be accessed from the intersection of State Route 99 and Territorial Road.  After 
approximately 8.3 miles from the intersection, access goes south on the County Maintained section of 
Bell Cow Road for approximately 1.5 miles when Bell Cow  Road turns into a private road, with site 
access granted via sub easement licenses with private landowners. 
 
 
ZONING DISTRICT: 
ARTICLE 3 – A-General  
 
Section 301 – Purpose  
 
The main purpose of the A-General Zoning District is to provide for all the unincorporated areas of the County, 
not otherwise designated for some other specific zone. No subdivision, as outlined in the Subdivision 
Regulations & Requirements, shall be conducted or approved in the A-General Zoning District without prior 
rezoning of the land intended to be subdivided. Uses permitted in the A-General Zoning District include farm 
and non-farm residential uses, farms, recreational, and institutional uses. 
 
ZONING ORDINANCE: 
Article 3 – A-General  
 
Section 302 – Use Regulations 
  
The following use requires a Special Use Permit within the A-General Zoning District:

<!-- page 1309 -->
Board of Supervisors              3 | P a g e  
 
 
20.  Television, wireless, and radio transmitter towers and stations. 
 
 
COMPREHENSIVE PLAN/AREA PLAN:  
Comprehensive Plan 
 
Land Use Goals and Policies 
 
Land Use Goal #1 
Accommodate and promote a balanced, efficient, aesthetic, and compact land development pattern with 
the appropriate level of services for water, wastewater, education, and public safety that is compatible 
with adjacent land uses, is well integrated with the transportation system, and is sensitive to the natural 
environment. 
• The proposed development is compatible with adjacent land uses.  The property is zoned 
as A-General allowing farms and all agricultural uses; the landowner plans to continue 
cattle grazing activities on the land during the operations of the MET tower and 
operational life of the prospective wind farm. 
 
Land Use Policy #1 
Navajo County supports continued coordination with federal, state, and local agencies to ensure a 
balanced mix of land uses in the region. 
• The applicant coordinated with the Arizona Game and Fish Department for review of the 
MET tower. 
 
Land Use Policy #16 
Navajo County supports development that provides buffers between different land uses, such as 
increased setbacks, walls, fences, and landscaping. 
• The applicant has provided increased setbacks.  Typical non-residential setbacks are 1:1.  
The smallest of the setbacks is 1,667.97 feet. 
 
 
Analysis: 
 
The proposed Special Use Permit  meets all relevant goals and policies of  the Navajo County Zoning 
Ordinance as described above. This project, and its submittal, meet all requirements of Article 3 of the 
Navajo County Zoning Ordinance, which regulates A-General.  
 
Planning and Development Services Staff have received twenty-nine (29) emails against, three (3) 
emails in support, and twelve (12) voicemails against the project as of January 20th, 2026. 
 
At the December 18 th, 2025  Navajo County Planning and Zoning Commission Hearing, the Navajo 
County Planning and Zoning Commission recommended approval of this Special Use Permit subject to 
the conditions recommended by Staff which are contained in this Staff Report.  
 
FINDINGS OF FACT: 
 
1. The proposal is in compliance with the Comprehensive Plan. 
 
The proposed project meets a ll applicable goals within Navajo County’s Comprehensive Plan, as 
noted within this report. 
 
2. The proposed use is compatible with the permissible uses in the zoning district in which 
the property is located.

<!-- page 1310 -->
Board of Supervisors              4 | P a g e  
 
 
The proposed use is compatible with permissible uses within the A-General zoning districts with a 
Special Use Permit. 
 
3. The proposed use is compatible with the current and likely future uses of properties in 
the vicinity of the proposed use.  
 
The proposed use complies with the Aztec Area Plan  under the Future Land Use Map .  The 
properties in the vicinity of this proposal are mainly utilized for cattle grazing.  Given the size of 
these properties, as well as the subject property, and the relatively small footprint of the 
meteorological tower, there should be no future compat ibility issues between uses on these 
properties. 
 
4. The proposed use will  have minimal adverse effects on the public health, safety, and 
general welfare of properties in the vicinity of the proposed use. 
 
Given the nature of the property and the zoning in the area, there should be minimal adverse effects 
on the public health, safety, and general welfare of properties in the vicinity of the proposed use. 
 
   
PLANNING AND DEVELOPMENT SERVICES RECOMMENDATION:  
 
Navajo County Planning and Development Services Staff recommend approval of the Special Use 
Permit, subject to the following conditions: 
 
1. This Special Use Permit shall allow for the installation of a meteorological tower, with a maximum 
height of 272 feet. 
 
2. The meteorological tower shall be erected only in the location indicated on the approved site plan, 
except as may otherwise be approved by the Navajo County Planning & Development Services 
Department. 
 
3. Building Permits are required for the meteorological tower and any accessory uses.  Any required 
permits shall be obtained prior to construction. 
 
4. The applicant shall meet all State and Federal requirements concerning towers prior to any Building 
Permits being issued. 
 
5. Concurrent with the submittal of an application for any building or related permits for the 
meteorological tower, the applicant shall provide information regarding the type of safety lighting that 
is proposed and confirmation that the safety lighting is in  conformance with FAA regulations.  All 
lighting, to the extent allowable by the FAA shall adhere to the following: 
 
a. The minimum number of lights shall be used. 
b. The use of low -intensity, red pulsating/blinking lighting is preferred, provided such lighting 
conforms to FAA regulations. 
c. The use of strobe-type lighting is prohibited unless expressly required by the FAA. 
 
6. A Floodplain Use Permit, if required, shall be obtained prior to issuance of any Building Permits. 
 
7. The meteorological tower and all guy -wire footings shall be enclosed by a security fence with a 
maximum height of 7 feet (excluding barbed wire or cyclone wire).  Information regarding who to 
contact in the event of an emergency or any problems with the to wer or its associated uses and 
structures shall be placed upon the fence.  The information shall include a contact name, company 
name, and phone number for someone who can be reached 24 hours a  day, 7 days a week.

<!-- page 1311 -->
Board of Supervisors              5 | P a g e  
 
8. Prior to acquiring a Building Permit, the applicant shall work with the Arizona Game and Fish 
Department to design their tower to comply with the following requirements: 
 
a. Install Bird Flight Diverters (BFDs) at regular intervals along the full length of all outer 
meteorological tower guy wires. 
b. Install Aircraft Warning Markers (AWMs) near the tops of all outer meteorological tower guy 
wires. 
c. Paint the top of the meteorological tower orange and white. 
d. Locate the meteorological tower away from cliffs, canyons, water sources, and other wildlife -
attracting features to the fullest extent possible. 
 
9. The applicant shall provide GPS locations of the final site of the meteorological tower to the Arizona 
Game and Fish Department, and to the Navajo County Planning & Development Services Department. 
 
10. The meteorological tower shall be located so that it will not fall onto adjacent property nor another 
structure in case of failure. 
 
11. Prior to issuance of any Building Permits for the meteorological tower, the developer shall submit to 
the Navajo County Planning & Development Services Department information regarding the 
manufacturer of the tower, structural information, and information regarding who to contact in the 
event of an emergency or any problems with the tower. 
 
12. If the permitted Special Use is not utilized within a twelve (12) month period from the date of approval 
by the Board of Supervisors, this permit shall become null and void. 
 
13. Within six (6) months after the tower ceases to be used, the applicant, at their sole expense, shall 
remove the tower and any accessories from the site. 
 
14. Development and use of the site shall include efforts, consistent with Best Management Practices, to 
reduce and mitigate dust created by this project.  Efforts shall also be made to reduce the removal of 
vegetation during construction and use of the site a nd any roadways that provide access to the site.  
Upon the removal of the meteorological tower and associated structures, the site and any roadways 
that provide access to the site shall be res tored and re -vegetated to their pre -disturbed/native 
condition by the applicant. 
 
15. This Special Use Permit shall be allowed to occur per the approved site plan.  Any expansion/change 
of the approved Special Use Permit shall require an amendment. 
 
16. This Special Use Permit shall be personal to the permittee and applicable only to the specific use and 
to the specific property for which it is issued.  Upon completion and final inspection by the Planning 
& Development Services Director (or designee) of any authorized structures, signifying that all zoning 
and site development requirements imposed in connection with the permit have been satisfied, the 
Special Use Permit shall thereafter be transferable and s hall run with the land, whereupon the 
maintenance of special conditions imposed by the permit, as well as the compliance with other 
provisions of this title, shall be the responsibility of the property owner/applicant. 
 
17. This Special Use Permit shall be reviewed on the fifth (5th) anniversary of Board Approval.

Chairman and Members of the Planning & Zoning Commission,   
 
We are the Civic Integrity Alliance of Northeast Arizona, representing concerned residents of Navajo 
County. We strongly oppose Agenda Item 5 – the Special Use Permit (SUP 25-004) for the proposed 272-
foot meteorological tower on parcel 111-07-003A, owned by Aztec Land & Cattle Company, Ltd., 
southwest of Joseph City.  
 
The application’s project narrative explicitly states that the MET tower is designed “to inform the energy 
assessment of a future potential wind energy generation facility” – the Winding Canyon Wind Farm, 
developed by Winding Canyon Wind Farm LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary of EDP Renewables North 
America LLC (EDPR NA). EDPR NA is headquartered in Houston, Texas, but is a subsidiary of the global 
EDP Renewables (a Portuguese-based multinational corporation).  
 
This tower is not a standalone, minor structure; it is the precursor to a large-scale industrial wind project 
on thousands of acres of privately owned ranch land in our rural high desert. The site is currently used for 
cattle grazing, which the applicant claims will continue alongside the tower.  
 
However, a 272-foot tubular tilt-up tower with extensive guy wires, anchors, and a lightning rod 
introduces incompatible industrial elements into the A-General zoned area, potentially interfering with 
ongoing agricultural operations, low-level aviation (common in ranching), and the open scenic character 
of the region. Arizona Game and Fish Department (AZGFD) comments, included as an attachment in the 
application, raise significant concerns about risks to birds, bats, and low-flying wildlife survey pilots. 
AZGFD recommends mandatory guidelines to minimize mortality, installation of a Motus telemetry 
tracking station, pre-construction surveys, and ongoing coordination.  
 
The applicant responds only with vague commitments to “continue to work with AZGFD” and “explore” 
optional measures like Motus – providing no binding protections or enforceable mitigation.  
 
Additionally:  
 • FAA review is pending (ASN 2025-WTW-11628-OE), with no final determination yet. 
• The tower could operate for up to seven years, but the application lacks a detailed decommissioning 
plan, performance bond, or guarantees for removal if the project stalls.     
 Some people who received this message don't often get email from kellymeixler@proton.me. Learn why this is important

<!-- page 1333 -->
2
 • No provisions address potential cumulative impacts from nearby renewable developments, such as 
the ongoing West Camp Wind Farm (a separate 500+ MW project in Navajo County).      
 
Approving this permit prematurely enables irreversible industrialization without adequate study of the 
full wind farm’s effects, including visual blight across our open landscapes, wildlife mortality 
(particularly to migratory birds, bats, and species like Golden Eagles), noise/shadow flicker, road 
degradation during any future construction, potential property value impacts, and strain on local 
infrastructure.  
 
Staff recommends approval with conditions, but these do not sufficiently address wildlife risks, aviation 
safety, decommissioning, or the tower’s role in facilitating a much larger project that could burden 
residents while primarily benefiting a multinational developer through federal subsidies and utility 
incentives.  
 
We respectfully urge the Commission to DENY SUP 25-004 or, at minimum, TABLE it indefinitely until: 
 • FAA issues final approval with enforceable conditions,      
 • Binding wildlife mitigation (including mandatory Motus station and pre-construction surveys) is 
incorporated,     
 • A comprehensive environmental review assesses cumulative impacts from Winding Canyon and 
surrounding projects, and     
 • Full public input is allowed on the broader wind farm proposal.      
 
Thank you for considering the long-term interests of Navajo County residents and protecting our rural 
way of life.  
 
Sincerely,  
Kelly Meixler, Celia Laughton, Lisa Vincenti, Rick Burris, Belinda Quog, Roger Gorres, MJ Coking, Jacque

Dear Planning and Zoning Commission Members, 
I am writing regarding the December 18, 2025 Planning and Zoning Commission meeting, specifically Item 5: SUP 25-
004 
– Winding Canyon Wind – MET Tower . 
I respectfully urge the Commission to delay or deny approval of this permit  until a full Environmental Impact 
Statement (EIS)  and a comprehensive environmental review of the entire proposed Winding Canyon Wind project  are 
completed and made available for public review. 
While this application concerns a MET tower, it is not an isolated action. The MET tower is an integral and enabling 
component of a much larger industrial wind development. Proceeding with permitting at this stage risks 
segmenting the 
project , effectively advancing development before the full environmental, wildlife, visual, cultural, and cumulative 
impacts of the entire wind farm have been properly evaluated. 
A complete EIS is necessary to assess, at minimum: 
• Impacts to wildlife, including birds and bats 
• Effects on sensitive habitats and ecosystems 
• Visual, noise, and community impacts 
• Cultural and archaeological resources 
• Cumulative impacts of the full build-out of the wind facility 
Approving incremental permits without a comprehensive review undermines transparency and limits meaningful public 
participation. Delaying or denying this permit until a full EIS is completed would ensure decisions are informed, legally 
sound, and consistent with responsible land-use planning. 
I respectfully ask the Commission to require a project-wide environmental review  before allowing any component of 
the Winding Canyon Wind project to move forward. 
Thank you for your time, consideration, and service to the community.

SUP 25-004 9
1.This SUP shall allow for the installation of a MET tower, with a max height of 272
feet.
2. The MET tower shall be erected only in the location indicated on the approved
site plan.
3. Building Permits are required for the MET tower and any accessory uses.
4. The applicant shall meet all State and Federal requirements concerning towers
prior to any Building Permits being issued.
5. The applicant shall provide information regarding the type of safety lighting in
conformance with FAA regulations.
6. A  Floodplain Use Permit, if required, shall be obtained prior to issuance of any
Building Permits.
7. The MET tower and all guy-wire footings shall be enclosed by a security fence

9. The applicant shall provide GPS locations of the final site of the MET tower to
the AZG&F Department and Planning & Development Services Department.
10. The MET tower shall be located so that it will not fall onto adjacent property
nor another structure in case of failure.
11. Prior to issuance of any Building Permits for the MET tower, the developer shall
submit information regarding the manufacturer of the tower, structural
information, and information regarding who to contact in the event of an
emergency or any problems with the tower.
12. If the permitted Special Use is not utilized within a 12-month period from the
date of approval by the BOS, this permit shall become null and void.
13. Within 6 months after the tower ceases to be used, the applicant, at their sole
expense, shall remove the tower and any accessories from the site. 
14. Upon the removal of the MET tower and associated structures, the site and any
roadways that provide access to the site shall be restored and re-vegetated to their
pre-disturbed/native condition by the applicant.
15. SUP shall be allowed to occur per approved site plan. Any expansion/change of
Special Use shall require amendment.
16. SUP is specific to permittee and property.
17. SUP shall be reviewed on 5th anniversary of Board Approval.

RESOLUTION ____-2026
A RESOLUTION OF THE NAVAJO COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS APPROVING
A SPECIAL USE PERMIT FOR WINDING CANYON WIND MET TOWER
WHEREAS, an application for a Special Use Permit for Winding Canyon Wind Met
Tower was duly filed on October 14 th, 2025, by Kevin Gooley to construct and operate one (1)
meteorological monitoring tower on approximately .7479 acres of vacant land in the Joseph City
area; and
WHEREAS, the application concerns the following real property in Navajo County:
APN # 111-07-003A, Township 16 North, Range 17 East, Section 05, 07, 09, 17 of the Gila and
Salt River Base and Meridian; and
WHEREAS, the application was considered by the Navajo County Planning & Zoning
Commission at a duly noticed public hearing on December 18, 2025; and
WHEREAS, the Navajo County Board of Supervisors after considering the testimony
and other evidence presented at the hearing, as well as the recommendations of staff, found that
the Special Use Permit is consistent with the public health, safety and general welfare and should
be approved subject to the conditions set forth herein; and
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED  the Board of Supervisors hereby
approves the Special Use Permit, subject to the following conditions:
1. This Special Use Permit shall allow for the installation of a meteorological tower, with a
maximum height of 272 feet.
2. The meteorological tower shall be erected only in the location indicated on the approved
site plan, except as may otherwise be approved by the Navajo County Planning &
Development Services Department.
3. Building Permits are required for the meteorological tower and any accessory uses.  Any
required permits shall be obtained prior to construction.
4. The applicant shall meet all State and Federal requirements concerning towers prior to
any Building Permits being issued.
5. Concurrent with the submittal of an application for any building or related permits for the
meteorological tower, the applicant shall provide information regarding the type of safety

<!-- page 1360 -->
Navajo County - For Official Use Only
lighting that is proposed and confirmation that the safety lighting is in conformance with
FAA regulations.  All lighting, to the extent allowable by the FAA shall adhere to the
following:
a. The minimum number of lights shall be used.
b. The use of low-intensity, red pulsating/blinking lighting is preferred, provided
such lighting conforms to FAA regulations.
c. The use of strobe-type lighting is prohibited unless expressly required by the
FAA.
6. A Floodplain Use Permit, if required, shall be obtained prior to issuance of any Building
Permits.
7. The meteorological tower and all guy-wire footings shall be enclosed by a security fence
with a maximum height of 7 feet (excluding barbed wire or cyclone wire).  Information
regarding who to contact in the event of an emergency or any problems with the tower or
its associated uses and structures shall be placed upon the fence.  The information shall
include a contact name, company name, and phone number for someone who can be
reached 24 hours a  day, 7 days a week.
8. Prior to acquiring a Building Permit, the applicant shall work with the Arizona Game and
Fish Department to design their tower to comply with the following requirements:
a. Install Bird Flight Diverters (BFDs) at regular intervals along the full length of all
outer meteorological tower guy wires.
b. Install Aircraft Warning Markers (AWMs) near the tops of all outer
meteorological tower guy wires.
c. Paint the top of the meteorological tower orange and white.
d. Locate the meteorological tower away from cliffs, canyons, water sources, and
other wildlife-attracting features to the fullest extent possible.
9. The applicant shall provide GPS locations of the final site of the meteorological tower to
the Arizona Game and Fish Department, and to the Navajo County Planning &
Development Services Department.
10. The meteorological tower shall be located so that it will not fall onto adjacent property
nor another structure in case of failure.
11. Prior to issuance of any Building Permits for the meteorological tower, the developer
shall submit to the Navajo County Planning & Development Services Department
information regarding the manufacturer of the tower, structural information, and
information regarding who to contact in the event of an emergency or any problems with
the tower.
12. If the permitted Special Use is not utilized within a twelve (12) month period from the
date of approval by the Board of Supervisors, this permit shall become null and void.

<!-- page 1361 -->

13. Within six (6) months after the tower ceases to be used, the applicant, at their sole
expense, shall remove the tower and any accessories from the site.

to reduce the removal of vegetation during construction and use of the site and any
roadways that provide access to the site.  Upon the removal of the meteorological tower
and associated structures, the site and any roadways that provide access to the site shall
be restored and re-vegetated to their pre-disturbed/native condition by the applicant.
15. This Special Use Permit shall be allowed to occur per the approved site plan.  Any

Background:
38-431.03. Executive sessions; definitions
A. On a public majority vote of the members constituting a quorum, a public body may hold an executive
session but only for the following purposes:
1. Discussion or consideration of employment, assignment, appointment, promotion, demotion, dismissal,
salaries, disciplining or resignation of a public officer, appointee or employee of any public body, except
that, with the exception of salary discussions, an officer, appointee or employee may demand that the
discussion or consideration occur at a public meeting. The public body shall provide the officer,
appointee or employee with written notice of the executive session as is appropriate but not less than

Background:
38-431.03. Executive sessions; definitions
A. On a public majority vote of the members constituting a quorum, a public body may hold an executive
session but only for the following purposes:
1. Discussion or consideration of employment, assignment, appointment, promotion, demotion, dismissal,
salaries, disciplining or resignation of a public officer, appointee or employee of any public body, except
that, with the exception of salary discussions, an officer, appointee or employee may demand that the
discussion or consideration occur at a public meeting. The public body shall provide the officer,
appointee or employee with written notice of the executive session as is appropriate but not less than
twenty-four hours for the officer, appointee or employee to determine whether the discussion or
consideration should occur at a public meeting
Recommendation:
